papers.title: Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits
papers.summary: We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.
papers.title_ja: 対称軌道のためのCR3BPにおけるMoser正則化：月軌道の分岐ネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 空間円周制限三体問題（CR3BP）における対称周期軌道の解析にMoser正則化を用いた計算フレームワークを提案する。この手法により、主天体との衝突をまたいで周期軌道族の数値的継続が可能となり、Floquet乗数や安定性指数も正則化座標系内で計算できる。地球-月系への適用により、Lyapunov軌道族やNRHO族からなる分岐ネットワークが明らかになり、これらはHill問題の限界における組織構造と整合する。さらに、Conley-Zehnder指数などのシンプレクティック不変量を用いて結果のトポロジー的整理を行う。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学・三体問題・軌道設計のコア領域であり、高度に専門的

papers.title: Cislunar navigation is an observability problem: arc-length thresholds, Gramian conditioning, and the Doppler lever
papers.summary: Dilution of precision is the standard way to describe navigation geometry and it does not apply in cislunar space: its derivation presumes a snapshot solution in which simultaneous measurements determine the state at one instant. A spacecraft tracked by inter-satellite ranging in the Earth-Moon three-body problem has no such solution: range is a function of position only, so the velocity columns of the measurement Jacobian vanish identically and the state is unobservable however many links are in view. The correct figure of merit is dynamical, because the three-body flow carries velocity information into later range measurements. We demonstrate this on four differential-corrected planar distant retrograde orbits, reporting the observability Gramian rather than a dilution of precision. Instantaneous range-only geometry has rank 2 of 4; the full state becomes observable only after a tracking arc of 2.09 h, the first sampled arc at full rank on a 0.26 h grid, and a square-root information filter recomputing the same quantity by a different route becomes well-posed at exactly that arc. Beyond it, conditioning improves monotonically with arc length, the Gramian condition number falling from 1.2e11 at 3 h to 1.4e5 at 48 h. Adding range rate lifts the instantaneous rank from 2 to 4, so a Doppler-capable link makes a snapshot solution exist where a range-only link cannot. Lifting the known-reference assumption, the joint problem of estimating a station and the satellites' states and clocks together is rank-deficient by exactly one without an external interferometric observable in all twenty realizations tested, and full rank with it; the deficiency persists only to four satellites. For the configurations studied, cislunar navigation requirements are better written as arc-length, conditioning and measurement-type budgets than as dilution-of-precision thresholds, which are undefined here.
papers.title_ja: シスルナ航行は観測可能性の問題である：弧長閾値、グラミアン条件数、およびドップラーレバー
papers.summary_ja: 地球-月三体問題におけるシスルナ空間では、従来の精度希釈係数（DOP）が適用できず、観測可能性の解析が必要である。本研究では、距離測定のみでは速度成分が観測不能だが、時間経過による軌道運動を通じて状態が観測可能になることを示した。観測弧長が約2.09時間を超えると状態が完全に観測可能になり、48時間ではグラミアンの条件数が大幅に改善されることを定量的に検証した。また、ドップラー測定（距離変化率）の追加により瞬時観測可能性が向上し、外部基準がない場合の位相干渉観測の必要性も明らかにした。
papers.relevance_reason: シスルナ軌道力学と観測可能性解析の組み合わせで、ユーザーの関心に直結

papers.title: LLM-Based Evaluation Planning for Heterogeneous Optimization
papers.summary: Heterogeneous optimization problems require an optimizer to decide not only which candidate solutions to evaluate, but also which objectives and constraints should be evaluated under different costs and fidelities. Existing SOTA methods such as MFE-NSGA-III address this setting with manually designed selection metrics, but their behavior is largely determined by predefined heuristic rules and hyperparameters. In this work, we propose REP-HO, a reasoning-based evaluation planner that replaces the rule-based mixed-fidelity selection step with a large language model (LLM) planner. The LLM receives the same primitive optimization-state information as the heuristic planner, such as surrogate predictions, uncertainties, evaluation costs, and budget status. We first show that REP-HO achieves competitive performance compared to the human-designed metric-based method (MFE-NSGA-III). We then further enhance each decision with an adaptive nearest-neighbor summary, leading to better and more stable results. We evaluate REP-HO across five heterogeneous regimes covering cost imbalance, constraint difficulty, surrogate fidelity, budget level, and objective conflict. Across these regimes, one of the two variants obtains the best mean ranking score in every regime, REP-HO(Deepseek) is first or second throughout, and the planner shows adaptive allocation behavior, such as prioritizing constraint evaluations under tighter budgets and reallocating constraint evaluation budget when surrogate reliability changes. These results suggest that LLMs can serve as flexible evaluation planners for heterogeneous optimization, offering a general alternative to fixed hand-designed metrics.
papers.title_ja: 異種最適化におけるLLMベースの評価計画
papers.summary_ja: 異種最適化問題において、どの候補解や目的関数を評価するかを決定するプロセスを、従来の手動設計されたヒューリスティックルールから大規模言語モデル（LLM）ベースのプランナーに置き換える手法「REP-HO」を提案する。LLMはサロゲート予測や不確実性、評価コストなどの情報を受け取り、予算制約やサロゲートの信頼性に応じて評価リソースを適応的に配分する。5つの異なる最適化シナリオでの評価により、既存のSOTA手法と同等以上の性能を示し、特に予算が厳しい状況下での制約評価の優先順位付けや、サロゲート信頼性変化時の予算再配分といった適応的な行動を確認した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMとサロゲートモデルを組み合わせた最適化手法であり、ユーザーの関心領域と高度に一致する。

papers.title: VBO-MI: A Differentiable Black-Box Optimization Framework via Variational Mutual Information Estimation
papers.summary: Many real-world tasks require optimizing expensive black-box functions accessible only through noisy evaluations, a setting commonly addressed with Bayesian optimization. While Gaussian processes(GPs) and Bayesian neural networks have driven significant progress, GP-based methods scale cubically with observations, and BNN-based approaches remain burdened by expensive posterior sampling such as Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, and inner-loop acquisition optimization in high-dimensional setting. In this work, we propose VBO-MI, a fully gradient-based BO framework that requires no assumptions on a Gaussian prior or a variational posterior family over $f$. While our framework uses gradient-based updates to train the internal action and information-estimation networks, it treats the objective function $f$ as a strict black box, requiring only zeroth-order evaluations. To enable end-to-end gradient flow, we employ an actor-critic architecture consisting of an action-net to navigate the input space and a variational critic to estimate a surrogate information signal for exploration. Additionally, we design a lightweight surrogate that approximates the objective from observed data using a replay buffer, which reduces the total required real function queries to one batch per iteration. We provide theoretical analysis for our framework, establishing convergence of its training objective and surrogate estimator, and showing, that near-optimal solutions exist. We evaluate our method on a diverse suite of benchmarks, including high-dimensional synthetic function and complex real-world tasks such as Rover Trajectory planning optimization, the Lunar Lander, and Pest Control problems. Our experiments demonstrate that VBO-MI provides the same or superior optimization performance over the various baselines.
papers.title_ja: VBO-MI: 変分相互情報推定による微分可能ブラックボックス最適化フレームワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、高次元なブラックボックス関数の最適化において、ガウス過程の計算コストやベイズニューラルネットのサンプリング負荷を解消する、完全な勾配ベースのベイズ最適化フレームワーク「VBO-MI」を提案する。アクター・クリティックアーキテクチャを用い、入力空間の探索と情報量推定を微分可能な形で統合し、リプレイバッファによる軽量サロゲートで実関数クエリを1イテレーションあたり1バッチに削減する。理論的に収束性と近似的最適解の存在を示し、ローバー軌道計画や月面着陸などの複雑な実世界タスクにおいて、既存手法と同等以上の性能を実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: ベイズ最適化と軌道計画の両方に深く関連し、効率化手法として高評価。

papers.title: FHKAN: Fractional Hermite Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Data-Driven and Physics-Informed Learning
papers.summary: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) replace fixed scalar weights by learnable univariate maps, yet most spectral KANs still rely on Chebyshev polynomials that live on a bounded interval and therefore require a saturating squashing of the pre-activation. We introduce the Fractional Hermite Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (FHKAN), a neural architecture that equips KANs with an adaptive, trainable fractional-order generalized Hermite basis. With a nonnegative shape parameter, the underlying generalized Hermite functions are orthonormal on the entire real line and uniformly bounded under a Gaussian envelope, so they act directly on unbounded pre-activations without any saturating map. We derive closed-form derivatives of the generalized, fractional, and scaled basis away from the origin and determine its order of differentiability at the origin, where the fractional power map creates a singular point. On synthetic regression, FHKAN attains the lowest test error at every network depth among nine fixed activations and the spline-based KAN. On image classification, image denoising, and sentiment analysis, the best-performing fractional Hermite block yields the highest accuracy or reconstruction quality. On physics-informed problems, FHKAN reaches mean absolute errors of order 10^-6 to 10^-5 on the Lane-Emden equation, residuals of order 10^-4 on the Burgers equation, and absolute errors below 10^-4 on a fractional delay differential equation.
papers.title_ja: FHKAN: データ駆動および物理情報学習のための分数階Hermite Kolmogorov-Arnoldネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、Kolmogorov-Arnoldネットワーク（KAN）の基底関数として、実数全域で定義される分数階一般化Hermite関数を導入した新アーキテクチャFHKANを提案する。従来のChebyshev多項式が有界区間を前提とするのに対し、FHKANは飽和マップなしで非有界な事前活性化に直接作用し、計算効率と表現力の向上を実現する。合成回帰や画像分類などのデータ駆動タスクで既存手法を上回る精度を示すとともに、Lane-Emden方程式やBurgers方程式などの物理情報ニューラルネット（PINN）問題において、極めて低い誤差（10^-6〜10^-5程度）を達成し、物理法則を学習する能力の高さを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理情報ニューラルネットとサロゲートモデルの精度向上に直結する手法

papers.title: The KV-Surgeon: Compensation-Aware Offline KV-Cache Compaction
papers.summary: Offline compaction of the key--value cache (KV-cache) reduces the cost of repeatedly querying a fixed context by constructing a smaller cache once and reusing it subsequently. The central challenge of compaction is deciding which cache entries to delete and which to retain. Existing methods score each candidate for deletion on its own, with the rest of the cache being held fixed. However, softmax renormalization of the attention operation couples these decisions in a nonlinear manner: removing one entry changes the attention weights of every remaining one. In this work, we introduce KV-Surgeon, which uses calibration data to take interactions into account in a tractable way. We derive a quadratic surrogate that admits closed-form expressions for jointly making the optimal greedy removal decision as well as compensation within the remaining entries. On QuALITY, LongHealth, and Long Code Arena, and at every evaluated compaction ratio, KV-Surgeon substantially advances the cost--accuracy Pareto frontier of dense and mixture-of-experts models from 4B to 30B parameters. At $50\times$ compaction, KV-Surgeon improves question-answering accuracy by up to four points over attention matching (Zweiger et al., 2026), the state of the art, at comparable cost. Lastly, we introduce an even faster variant, which also exceeds the state of the art while requiring only two fifths of its cost.
papers.title_ja: KV-Surgeon: 補償を考慮したオフラインKVキャッシュ圧縮
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMのKVキャッシュをオフラインで圧縮し、推論コストを削減する手法「KV-Surgeon」を提案する。既存手法がエントリ削除を独立に判断するのに対し、アテンションのsoftmax再正規化による非線形な結合効果を考慮し、二次近似サロゲートモデルを用いて最適な削除と残存エントリの補償を閉形式で導出する。QuALITYなどのベンチマークにおいて、4B〜30Bパラメータのモデルでコストと精度のパレートフロンティアを大幅に改善し、50倍圧縮時でも既存手法より最大4ポイント精度を向上させることを示した。さらに、コストを5分の2に抑えつつSOTAを超える高速版も提案している。

papers.title: A Probabilistic, Rotation-Preserving Kernel Operator Surrogate for Continuum-Robot Design Spaces
papers.summary: We develop an uncertainty-aware, operator-learning-based surrogate for tendon-driven continuum robots (TDCRs) that generalizes across robot design and actuation while predicting the complete equilibrium configuration. Our central idea is a nonstationary Gaussian-process (GP) kernel whose metric is learned by a shallow neural network from mechanics-aware design coordinates. The network learns how similarity changes across design space, while the resulting kernel defines the design-to-pose operator, its posterior uncertainty, and a criterion for sequential simulator acquisition. We represent backbone position and rotational strain with spatial kernels and reconstruct orientation directly on SO(3), preserving valid material frames and tendon geometry. We use ASkotch with Nystrom preconditioning for scalable kernel operator solves and a separate Nystrom approximation for posterior covariance. Experiments show that kernel-coverage acquisition reduces mean trajectory error by approximately 15% relative to IID sampling, while posterior variance increases for increasingly unsupported designs. Compared with prior neural-operator TDCR models, the method is 30-50% more accurate using approximately 5x fewer training designs while additionally providing posterior uncertainty estimates.
papers.title_ja: 連続体ロボット設計空間のための確率的・回転保持カーネルオペレータサロゲート
papers.summary_ja: 腱駆動型連続体ロボット（TDCR）の設計空間全体で汎化し、完全な平衡姿勢を予測する不確実性認識型サロゲートモデルを提案する。浅いニューラルネットワークで学習されたメトリックを用いた非定常ガウス過程カーネルにより、設計空間における類似性の変化を捉え、姿勢と回転ひずみをSO(3)上で直接再構成することで物理的制約を維持する。Nystrom事前条件付けを用いたASkotchによりスケーラブルなカーネルオペレータ解を計算し、後方分散に基づく逐次シミュレータ取得戦略を実装した。実験では、IIDサンプリング比で約15%の軌道誤差低減と、既存のニューラルオペレータモデル比で約5分の1の訓練設計数ながら30-50%高い精度と後方不確実性推定を実現した。

papers.title: Reconstruction of Unobserved Core Electron Density in Tokamak Plasmas with a Neural Operator Transport Surrogate and Uncertainty Quantification
papers.summary: Real-time control of tokamak plasmas requires the electron density profile. However, in a reactor-relevant device, diagnostic port access is limited and the profile can be observed only partially. In the present work we reconstruct the density profile by inferring the coefficients of a physics-based one-dimensional particle transport equation, using a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) surrogate of the transport solver as a fast differentiable forward model. The surrogate enables realtime-compatible gradient-based reconstruction and uncertainty quantification from the reflectometry and interferometry measurements. We compare four uncertainty quantification methods - multi-seed ensembles, the Laplace approximation, Metropolis-Hastings, and a Gaussian method independent of the reconstruction fit. The resulting uncertainty is scored with CRPS and coverage calibration, separately on the observed and unobserved regions. We further demonstrate advantage of our approach over standard analytical function fit on synthetic and experimental DIII-D discharges.
papers.title_ja: ニューラルオペレータ輸送サロゲートと不確実性定量化を用いたトカマクプラズマの未観測コア電子密度再構成
papers.summary_ja: トカマクプラズマの電子密度プロファイル再構成において、物理ベースの1次元粒子輸送方程式の係数を推定する手法を提案する。Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) を用いた輸送ソルバーのサロゲートモデルにより、リアルタイム対応可能な勾配ベースの再構成と不確実性定量化を実現した。マルチシードアンサンブル、ラプラス近似、メトロポリス・ハースティングス法、ガウス法という4つの不確実性定量化手法を比較し、CRPS とカバレッジキャリブレーションで評価した。合成データおよび DIII-D 実験データにおいて、従来の解析的関数フィッティング手法を上回る性能を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: ニューラルオペレータとサロゲートモデルによる物理シミュレーション高速化と不確実性定量化が関心と一致

papers.title: The Segal-Bargmann Transform in Neural Partial Differential Equations
papers.summary: We introduce a novel neural operator method based on Segal-Bargmann transform and Bargmann-Fock space for learning the solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs). The method brings data encoding, latent-space representation, operator learning, and decoding into an unifed framework. From only finitely many observations, we establish a sup-norm reconstruction error of order $ L^{-\frac{1}{2}} $, where L is the number of complex sampling points that are decoupled with the original samplings and observations. The reconstruction error is independent of the spatial dimension and the number of original sampling points. We show that this new mesh-free Segal-Bargmann Neural Operator approach has superior performance compared to existing NO approaches like FNO, BelNet, GNOT, etc.,\ particularly in terms of pointwise control $ \sup_{x}\lvert\hat{u}_{NO} - u_{truth}\rvert $ for solutions of PDEs $ \mathcal{L}u = f $ which provides pointwise accuracy and interpretability as classical numerical solvers. We also demonstrates the reconstructions of the solution operators for higher dimensional nonlinear PDEs, which suggest that our proposed method has great potential to be applied to more challenging PDEs and to even higher spatial dimensions.
papers.title_ja: ニューラル偏微分方程式におけるセガル・バーグマン変換
papers.summary_ja: セガル・バーグマン変換とバーグマン・フォック空間に基づいた新しいニューラルオペレータ手法を提案する。この手法は、データエンコーディングから復号までを統一した枠組みで扱い、空間次元やサンプリング点数に依存しない再構成誤差を理論的に保証する。既存のFNOやGNOTなどの手法と比較し、特に点ごとの精度（sup-norm）において優れた性能を示す。高次元非線形偏微分方程式の解演算子の再構成にも成功し、より複雑なPDEへの適用可能性を示唆している。
papers.relevance_reason: ニューラルオペレータとPDE解法の高速化・高精度化という関心領域に直結する。

papers.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Native NVFP4 promises to accelerate reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs), but achieving stable learning across separate training and sampling engines remains challenging. We show that matching model weights and numerical formats is insufficient to ensure consistent policy evaluation, highlighting the importance of cross-engine numerical execution. We introduce miniTE, a lightweight framework that combines execution diagnostics, cross-engine numerical alignment, and efficient native W4A4 (4-bit weights and activations) GEMM computation for LLM RL. It improves numerical execution consistency without modifying the RL objective, while reducing implementation overhead to realize the benefits of native low-bit computation. Long-horizon RL experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B demonstrate stable training and benchmark performance close to BF16, outperforming naive Transformer Engine (TE) NVFP4 in evaluation quality. On single NVIDIA B300 GPU node, the optimized learner reaches 33,540 tokens/s, yielding 1.39x and 1.47x the throughput of BF16 and TE NVFP4, respectively, for complete learner updates. We released the framework, kernels, diagnostics, and training configurations to make native low-bit RL easier.
papers.title_ja: miniTE: ネイティブNVFP4強化学習における実行ギャップの診断と橋渡し
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）の強化学習において、ネイティブNVFP4（4bit）量子化による安定した学習を妨げる「実行ギャップ」を診断し、解決する軽量フレームワークminiTEを提案する。モデル重みの一致だけでなく、学習エンジンとサンプリングエンジン間の数値実行の整合性が重要であることを示し、クロスエンジンの数値アライメントと効率的なW4A4 GEMM計算を実装した。Qwen3-30B-A3Bを用いた実験では、BF16に近い品質を保ちつつ、単一GPUノードでBF16比1.39倍、既存のTransformer Engine NVFP4比1.47倍のスループット向上を実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの量子化・推論高速化・RL効率化の核心を突く

papers.title: Factorization-Guided Training and Inference for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding
papers.summary: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference through parallel verification of tokens proposed by a drafter. Diffusion drafters further parallelize proposal generation, but greater proposal capacity or higher mean accepted tokens (MAT) need not yield higher throughput. Because verification accepts only a consecutive prefix, early rejections can render later correct predictions ineffective, limiting MAT gains, while even higher MAT may not improve throughput if per-round latency increases. We introduce DScout, which uses two complementary factorizations to guide diffusion drafter training and inference for higher throughput. For training, DScout factorizes position-wise loss into inclusion, weighting, and prediction loss. This guides the design and combination of mixed-horizon training, intra-block unmasking, and acceptance-weighted loss to align supervision with prefix acceptance and improve MAT. For inference, DScout factorizes throughput as the ratio of MAT to per-round latency, guiding target-conditioning depth, drafter depth, and inference block size selection to identify a high-throughput configuration for each workload. Across six benchmarks, DScout achieves $3.84\times$ and $4.14\times$ mean speedups over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, respectively, improving mean speedup over the state-of-the-art baseline by 9.1% and 7.1%. Across models and concurrency settings, our inference configuration policy provides up to 9.75% additional mean speedup over DScout's fixed configuration.
papers.title_ja: 拡散モデルによるドラフト生成を用いた投機的デコーディングのための、分解に基づく学習と推論
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、大規模言語モデル（LLM）の推論高速化技術である投機的デコーディングにおいて、拡散モデルをドラフターとして用いる際の効率化手法「DScout」を提案する。学習段階では、損失関数を位置ごとの包含・重み付け・予測損失に分解し、プレフィックスの受容率と整合させることで平均受容トークン数（MAT）を向上させる。推論段階では、スループットをMATと1ラウンドあたりのレイテンシの比として分解し、ワークロードに応じた最適な設定（ブロックサイズや深さなど）を自動選択する。Qwen3モデルを用いた実験では、自己回帰デコーディング比で最大4.14倍の高速化を実現し、既存の最先端手法よりも9.1%高い平均高速化率を達成した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化と効率化の核心技術であり、ユーザーの関心と完全に一致する。

papers.title: PeekKV: The First Content Token Already Knows Which Heads Matter
papers.summary: The size of the KV cache grows linearly with context length, making it a major memory bottleneck in LLM serving. Motivated by recent progress in identifying the functional roles of attention heads, a growing body of work compresses the KV cache non-uniformly across heads. Existing methods either fix the important heads via offline profiling or select them using attention signals from the prefill stage. In both cases, however, accuracy fluctuates substantially across workloads. While investigating the cause of this instability, we find that the active heads shift between the prefill and decode stages even within a single input. Along the decode path, by contrast, the activehead composition remains stable across content tokens once format tokens are filtered out. Based on this observation, we propose PeekKV. PeekKV observes a single content token immediately after prefill - a one-token peek - to jointly obtain head-group scores and token-importance scores. Guided by these scores, PeekKV allocates KV cache budgets to head groups in proportion to their group scores and retains only the top-scoring tokens within each budget. PeekKV requires no offline profiling or training and thus applies directly to unseen workloads and new models. Across four public benchmarks, PeekKV achieves the highest accuracy in more than half of the per-model comparisons against state-of-the-art methods, and stays closest to the full-cache accuracy on RULER and LongBench. On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, PeekKV retains 95.7% of the full-cache accuracy at a 10% memory budget on RULER with 16K contexts and 95.9% at a 1.5% budget on LongBench.
papers.title_ja: PeekKV: 最初のコンテンツトークンがどのヘッドが重要かを知っている
papers.summary_ja: LLMサービングにおけるKVキャッシュのメモリボトルネックを解決するため、アテンションヘッドの役割に基づいた非一様な圧縮手法を提案する。既存手法がオフラインプロファイリングやプリフィル段階のシグナルに依存し精度が不安定になる問題に対し、デコード段階でアクティブなヘッド構成が安定するという観察に基づく。PeekKVはプリフィル直後の1トークンだけを観察し、ヘッドグループとトークンの重要度スコアを算出することで、メモリ予算を動的に配分する。オフライン学習不要であり、RULERやLongBenchなどのベンチマークで、少ないメモリ予算下でもフルキャッシュに近い精度を維持することを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化・KVキャッシュ圧縮というユーザーの関心と直接一致

papers.title: How Data Scales in Agentic Reinforcement Learning: Laws and Synthesis Strategies
papers.summary: Pretraining scaling laws treat training data as a one-dimensional quantity: a token count. Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) inherits this scalar abstraction, but modern synthesis pipelines now generate \textit{tasks}, \textit{environments}, and \textit{trajectories} independently and at very different costs, turning data into a structured design space. This raises a question pretraining never had to answer: given a synthesis budget, \textit{which axis} should be scaled? We address this question end-to-end with three tightly coupled contributions. First, we decompose agentic data into three cardinality axes (task, environment, trajectory), plus a reward-density control variable, and fit per-axis scaling relations on different large language models (LLMs) across math+code, SWE, web, and UI/tool application domains. Across all model sizes, model families, domains, and RL algorithms (PPO and GRPO) we measured, the scaling exponents order as environment $>$ task $>$ trajectory. When environment diversity is decomposed into world and environment-structure diversity, its advantage is mainly driven by the former, while the latter is just comparable to the task diversity. Second, we use the fitted laws as a common ruler to price synthesis methods, capturing each method's efficiency as a per-axis discount factor and identifying critical synthetic-to-real ratios at which collapse begins; these ratios differ by an order of magnitude across axes. Third, we cast budget allocation as a constrained optimization under our laws and discounts, deriving a Chinchilla-style compute-optimal recipe and validating it at held-out scale. The empirical results demonstrate that following the recipe yields up to $1.7\times$ compute efficiency over the dominant ``scale-the-trajectories'' practice.
papers.title_ja: エージェント型強化学習におけるデータのスケーリング則と合成戦略
papers.summary_ja: エージェント型強化学習において、タスク・環境・軌道の3軸を独立した設計変数として捉え、それぞれのスケーリング則を導出した。環境多様性が最も効率的であることを示し、合成データと実データ比率の崩壊閾値を特定した。これらを基に計算資源配分の最適化モデルを構築し、既存手法比で最大1.7倍の計算効率向上を実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM強化学習のデータ効率化と最適化手法が関心に直結

papers.title: LatLM: Line-Parallel Language Models with Deferred Commitment
papers.summary: Line-parallel language models advance multiple lines concurrently for substantial speedups. However, frameworks like the Line-Coupled Language Model (LCLM) enforce a fixed commitment schedule across lines. Because dependencies vary within text, a fixed schedule cannot hold back a line whose prerequisites remain uncomputed, forcing premature commitments and cascading reasoning errors. To address this limitation, we introduce the Lattice Language Model (LatLM), making commitment schedules an adaptive decoding-time choice. Text occupies a 2D lattice where eligible frontier tokens are scored each round; a policy commits confident candidates while deferring unready ones for extended context. One forward pass supervises entire sampled trajectories via 2D causal masking, while an append-only cache retains exact states. At 482M parameters, we establish two findings. (1) LatLM matches a data- and capacity-matched autoregressive model on held-out text when decoded sequentially, while its adaptive parallel decoder achieves near-autoregressive accuracy on independent-line tasks using 25--41% as many decoding rounds. (2) When cross-line dependencies cause LCLM's fixed schedule to fail, deferred commitment substantially improves accuracy while retaining parallelism where dependencies permit. On mixed dependency chains, LatLM achieves 96.5% accuracy versus LCLM's 78.5%, using fewer than half the decoding rounds of the autoregressive baseline.
papers.title_ja: LatLM: 遅延コミットメントによる行並列言語モデル
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、行並列言語モデルにおける固定スケジュールの限界を克服するため、デコード時に適応的にコミットメントを決定するLatLMを提案する。テキストを2次元格子として扱い、信頼できるトークンを優先的に確定させ、依存関係が未解決のトークンはコンテキスト拡張を待って遅延させる仕組みを採用している。482Mパラメータのモデルで検証した結果、自己回帰モデルと同等の精度を維持しつつ、デコードラウンド数を25〜41%に削減できることを示した。特に行間の依存関係が複雑なタスクでは、固定スケジュール方式より大幅に精度を向上させつつ高速推論を実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化と効率化の核心手法であり、ユーザーの関心と直接一致する。

papers.title: PolyGraph: Plan-Buffered CUDA Graphs for Adaptive Speculative Decoding
papers.summary: Adaptive speculative decoding changes the active batch size B and draft length d from one decode step to the next, whereas a CUDA Graph replays a fixed launch configuration. The resulting verification width M = B d forces serving systems to pre-capture many shapes, capture new ones on the serving path, or pad every step to the largest draft. We present PolyGraph, a plan-buffer mechanism for custom Triton kernels that avoids this choice. PolyGraph captures one maximum-grid graph and writes the active shape to GPU memory before each replay. Kernels skip tiles beyond that shape, while graph topology, allocations, layouts, pointers, and launch grids remain fixed; the update transfers only 28 bytes. On one NVIDIA H800, a trace-driven prototype with Qwen2.5-3B dimensions replaces 64 shape-specific graphs with one, matches the warmed baseline in observed step latency (17.7 vs. 17.8 ms P50), and reduces measured pre-serving graph-build time from 3,915 to 93 ms. Fixed-draft controls show that the benefit comes from avoiding padded payload: the P99 difference from MaxPad is negligible at zero padding waste but reaches an 18.7% reduction at 100% waste. Our evidence establishes a bounded work-shape mechanism for custom kernels, not a production serving system, and is limited to synthetic traces on one GPU.
papers.title_ja: PolyGraph: 適応型投機的デコーディングのためのプランバッファリングCUDAグラフ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、バッチサイズやドラフト長が動的に変化する適応型投機的デコーディングにおいて、CUDAグラフの固定構成との不整合を解消する仕組みを提案する。最大グリッドサイズで1つのグラフをキャプチャし、実行時にGPUメモリへアクティブな形状情報を書き込むことで、不要なタイル処理をスキップしつつグラフトポロジーを固定する。これにより、多数の形状別グラフの事前構築を不要にし、サービング開始前のグラフ構築時間を大幅に短縮する。H800上のプロトタイプでは、ベースラインと同等のステップレイテンシを維持しつつ、構築時間を約40分の1に削減した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化とCUDA最適化の核心技術であり、ユーザーの関心と高度に一致する。

papers.title: Paired-Outcome Learning for Selective Spacecraft Attitude Capture under Torque Limits
papers.summary: Torque-limited spacecraft attitude capture requires adapting the maneuver speed to uncertain braking authority. Faster settings can reduce average tracking error while worsening individual maneuvers, making selective modification of an existing controller a baseline-relative learning problem. A paired-outcome method combines three mechanisms: physically interpretable continuation policies with different speed envelopes, separate prediction of task failure and successful-pair tracking gains, and context-dependent rejection that executes the unchanged baseline. Complete paired simulations provide labels under common plant parameters and measurement seeds; training, validation, and calibration are separated by context. Basilisk experiments use 108 development contexts, 324 labeling rollouts, and 624 evaluation episodes across 48 test contexts, including disclosed post-freeze diagnostics. The selective controller reduces aggregate integrated attitude error by 4.67% relative to the branch baseline, with 17 improvements, 31 exact ties, and no observed regressions. Always using the fast alternative achieves a 4.81% reduction but worsens 11 cases. Gains occur in principal-axis, near-axis, braking-boundary, and selected noise/drift maneuvers; general coupled cases retain the baseline. Ablations show no additional aggregate benefit from branch commitment, active querying, or score subtraction. The evidence supports a restricted empirical trade-off between average improvement and individual regression, without establishing a closed-loop safety guarantee.
papers.title_ja: トルク制限下での選択的宇宙機姿勢捕獲のためのペアリングアウトカム学習
papers.summary_ja: トルク制限のある宇宙機の姿勢制御において、既存のベースラインコントローラを安全に改善するための「ペアリングアウトカム学習」手法を提案する。物理的に解釈可能な継続ポリシーと、タスク失敗および成功時の追従ゲインを個別に予測し、文脈依存の拒否機構によりベースラインを維持する。シミュレーション実験では、集計された姿勢誤差を4.67%低減しつつ、個々のケースでの性能劣化（リグレッション）をゼロに抑えることを実証した。この手法は、平均的な性能向上と個別ケースの安全性のトレードオフを管理する実務的なアプローチを示している。
papers.relevance_reason: 宇宙機軌道・姿勢制御と機械学習（強化学習的アプローチ）の組み合わせであり、ユーザーの関心領域に直結する。

papers.title: A coupling normal form for reversible center-center Hamiltonians with application to the restricted three-body problem
papers.summary: Near a reversible center-center equilibrium, the Birkhoff normal form does not describe the families bifurcating from the continued tori, which resonant normal forms capture through a reduced system.With a reflection symmetry, we develop a coupling normal form in which the bifurcating families also appear as tori of action normal forms. Along a selected coupling direction, the first harmonic in the angle difference is absorbed into an action-dependent counterterm. We prove that the coupled recursion determines unique counterterm coefficients, a formal action normal form, and an exact counterterm factorization. The factorization gives a recovery constraint, whose trivial factor corresponds to the Birkhoff normal form. At every finite order, a symmetric pair of bifurcating branches leaves the trivial branch at a critical curve, carrying approximately invariant tori and circles with residual estimates. In the spatial circular restricted three-body problem, these give approximate halo orbits and quasi-halo tori.
papers.title_ja: 可逆な中心-中心ハミルトニアンに対する結合正規形と制限三体問題への応用
papers.summary_ja: 可逆な中心-中心平衡点付近において、分岐する軌道族を記述するために結合正規形を提案する。反射対称性を活用し、角度差の第1調波を作用依存の補正項に吸収することで、分岐する族も作用正規形のトーラスとして現れるようにする。この手法を用いると、空間円制限三体問題において、ハロー軌道や準ハロートーラスの近似解を効率的に導出できることを示す。
papers.relevance_reason: 制限三体問題の軌道設計・解析に直接関連する高度な数学的手法

papers.title: On the Hausdorff dimension of oscillatory motions in three-body problems
papers.summary: We show that for the Sitnikov example and for the restricted planar circular 3-body problem the set of oscillatory motions often has maximal Hausdorff dimension. Also, we construct Newhouse domains for both problems.
papers.title_ja: 三体問題における振動運動のハウスドルフ次元について
papers.summary_ja: シトニクフ問題および制限平面円周三体問題において、振動運動の集合が多くの場合最大ハウスドルフ次元を持つことを示した。また、両問題に対してニューハウス領域を構成し、カオス的振る舞いの構造を解析した。
papers.relevance_reason: ユーザーの関心である三体問題・軌道力学の理論的基礎に直結する

papers.title: The EMA Justitia Probe: Terminator Frame-Based Deployment Orbit Selection and Surface Coverage Analysis
papers.summary: The Emirates Mission to the Asteroid Belt (EMA) probe is designed to perform asteroid imaging during an uncontrolled ballistic descent to (269) Justitia. The mission design is constrained by main spacecraft proximity operations, uncertain asteroid gravity, limited knowledge of the final deployment trajectory, and requirements for illumination and safe operations. These constraints necessitate a mission design that ensures suitable illumination, attitude determination and control, and payload pointing throughout descent. The EMA probe concept of operations employs near-terminator deployment orbit geometry with continuous Sun visibility and two attitude control modes: single-axis Sun-spin for periodic imaging opportunities and three-axis asteroid-pointing for continuous asteroid visibility. Based on these modes, formal requirements are derived for deployment orbits that enable asteroid observations during ballistic descent. A deployment orbit selection method is developed using the terminator reference frame and a minimum boresight deviation margin. The method identifies families of orbit orientations satisfying illumination and payload observation constraints. Reference orbits are selected and verified through mission geometry analysis and trajectory propagation using a polyhedron gravity model. Asteroid surface coverage is then evaluated for uncontrolled tumbling, Sun-spin, and asteroid-pointing modes. The results characterize the expected imaging performance and demonstrate the feasibility of the EMA probe concept for close-proximity asteroid imaging. The proposed approach can also support future ballistic probe missions subject to similar operational and observational constraints.
papers.title_ja: EMA Justitia探査機：終線フレームに基づく展開軌道の選択と表面カバレッジ解析
papers.summary_ja: 小惑星(269) Justitiaへの無制御降下による撮影ミッションにおいて、終線（昼夜境界線）フレームを基準とした展開軌道の選択手法を提案する。太陽の可視性とペイロードの観測制約を満たす軌道族を特定し、多面体重力モデルを用いた軌道伝播で検証した。無制御回転、太陽同期、小惑星指向の各モードにおける表面カバレッジを評価し、近接撮影の可行性を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学・軌道設計・小惑星探査の核心テーマであり、ユーザーの関心と高度に一致する。

papers.title: Conformal Prediction-Enabled Sequence-level Policy Optimization for Reasoning Language Models
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning improves the reasoning capability of large language models through verifiable rewards for mathematical and coding tasks. In token-level methods such as GRPO, clipping acts on individual token ratios while the reward and advantage apply to a complete response. Recent sequence-level methods align these units but still use fixed clipping bands, whose tail probabilities change as the score distribution evolves. We propose Conformal Prediction-Enabled Sequence-level Policy Optimization (CSPO), which adaptively calibrates sequence-level clipping bounds using recent training statistics. The resulting band targets a specified marginal tail budget and adapts to policy drift; calibration conditional on response length requires additional assumptions. We bound the probability that a fresh score falls outside the band by the target miscoverage level plus explicit CDF discrepancy and drift terms. Under additional moment conditions, this bound also controls the objective and gradient error relative to the unclipped GSPO power surrogate. Experiments with the Qwen3-1.7B series show improvements over GSPO on difficult mathematical reasoning benchmarks and ALFWorld, with clipping endpoints that adapt during training.
papers.title_ja: 推論言語モデルのための、適合予測（Conformal Prediction）を活用したシーケンスレベルのポリシー最適化
papers.summary_ja: 強化学習によるLLMの推論能力向上において、トークンレベルのクリッピングが報酬単位と不一致を起こす問題を解決するため、シーケンスレベルでクリッピング境界を適応的に調整する手法CSPOを提案する。この手法は、直近の学習統計量を用いて適合予測に基づきクリッピング帯域を較正し、ポリシードリフトやスコア分布の変化に対応する。理論的には、クリッピングによる目的関数や勾配の誤差を明示的な項で有界化し、Qwen3-1.7Bを用いた実験では、困難な数学推論ベンチマークおよびALFWorldにおいて既存手法GSPOを上回る性能を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論強化とRL手法の改善であり、ユーザーの関心領域に直結する。

papers.title: Selecting the Best Few with Human Evaluators: Adaptively Combining Ratings and Pairwise Comparisons
papers.summary: This paper considers a decision-maker tasked with identifying the $k$ best items from a large pool of candidates, such as job applicants, LLMs, award nominees, or new product ideas. The decision-maker learns about the items' quality by soliciting human evaluations. Each evaluation can be costly, so the decision-maker aims to use the limited evaluation budget efficiently by allocating evaluations adaptively. A key consideration is the form of evaluation to solicit, which should be something evaluators are comfortable providing. Two popular forms are ratings and pairwise comparisons, and we allow for both, as they may be especially useful in combination given the limited budget. Ratings can be used early on to get a coarse picture of which items are good and which are not. As that picture forms, comparisons can refine the ordering of the good items, narrowing in on the ultimate top-$k$ selection. To solve the allocation problem, we develop an adaptive algorithm built from two allocation policies. The first, our primary contribution, is based on a surrogate objective that is naturally forward-looking, valuing evaluations that help inform what to evaluate in future rounds, not just those that directly improve the selection decision. The decision rule is interpretable, and we prove that it is asymptotically consistent. Late in the evaluation process, when being forward-looking is less productive, we construct a myopic policy and a criterion for switching to it. In simulation, the method gives insight into how to combine these two types of evaluations, and beats the (limited) existing benchmarks.
papers.title_ja: 人間評価者による最良の少数選定：評価とペアワイズ比較の適応的組み合わせ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMや応募者などの候補群から最良のk個を効率的に特定するための適応的評価戦略を提案する。コストの高い人間評価を節約するため、初期段階では粗い全体像を得るための「評価（レーティング）」、後期段階では上位候補の順位を精緻化する「ペアワイズ比較」を段階的に組み合わせる。主要貢献である先見性のあるサロゲート目的関数に基づく割り当てポリシーは、将来の評価に役立つ情報を重視し、漸近的一貫性を証明している。シミュレーションにより、既存ベンチマークを上回る性能と、2つの評価形式を最適に組み合わせるための洞察が示された。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM評価・ベンチマーク設計と適応的実験設計の最適化に直結

papers.title: Teacher Supervision, Fixed Representations and Calibration: Exact Risk Calculations for Candidate-Scoring Decision Models
papers.summary: Candidate-scoring decision models return a probability distribution over a presented set of answers. Public documentation of one such system, Jev, and of an open counterpart, JevAny, describes three training ingredients that determine what these probabilities estimate: soft targets from larger models, a frozen pretrained backbone and temperature calibration. We analyze each ingredient in Gaussian surrogates where the finite-sample risk can be computed exactly. A student trained on teacher targets inherits the teacher's bias, which more student data does not remove and agreement with the teacher does not reveal. A fixed representation lowers the risk only below an explicit sample-size threshold. In a probit model the exact recalibration map is a temperature scaling, which removes all excess risk only when the teacher's coefficient has the correct direction and otherwise leaves a residual that calibration diagnostics do not detect. Under Luce's choice axiom, candidate scores are coherent across refinements of an event if and only if they aggregate by log-sum-exp. On 231,521 credit card complaints from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, where the decision is whether a complaint ends in monetary relief, a student trained on a logistic teacher's probabilities ends at the teacher's decision cost while a student trained on outcomes goes 8% below it, a 30B model read zero-shot remains worse than the teacher after recalibration, and that model departs from the coherence condition by 17.5 decibans. Pretrained representations reduce the labeled data required and calibration corrects the scale of the probabilities, but neither corrects a biased teacher, so the probabilities have to be checked against realized outcomes.
papers.title_ja: 教師の監督、固定表現、キャリブレーション：候補スコアリング決定モデルにおける正確なリスク計算
papers.summary_ja: 候補スコアリング決定モデルの学習要素（教師モデルからのソフトターゲット、固定された事前学習済みバックボーン、温度キャリブレーション）をガウスサロゲートモデルを用いて解析し、有限サンプルリスクを厳密に計算した。教師のバイアスは生徒モデルのデータ量増加や教師との一致度では除去できず、固定表現はサンプルサイズ閾値以下でのみリスク低減に寄与することが示された。さらに、確率モデルにおける再キャリブレーションの正確なマップが温度スケーリングであることを証明し、教師の係数方向が誤っている場合、キャリブレーション診断では検出されない残留リスクが残ることを指摘した。実データ（クレジットカード苦情）での検証では、教師の確率を学習したモデルは教師の決定コストに収束する一方、結果を直接学習したモデルの方が8%低いコストを示し、事前学習表現とキャリブレーションはバイアス除去には不十分であることが確認された。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルとLLM効率化・評価手法の交差点で、実務的インパクトが高い

papers.title: Parameter misspecification in physics-informed neural networks: A closed-form audit and its limits
papers.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are trained to minimize the residual of a prescribed equation, so a low training loss does not indicate whether a coefficient in that equation was specified incorrectly. This study evaluates what can be inferred about the encoded parameter from the trained network alone. When the residual is linear in the parameter, written as $A - \nu B$, the least-squares estimate $\hat{\nu} = A^{\top}B/B^{\top}B$ is obtained from a single evaluation of the frozen network, without retraining or reference data. Its accuracy depends on how closely the network satisfies its own equation, quantified by a normalized residual $\rho$. Recovery error is associated with $\rho$ (log-log correlation 0.72 across 36 convection-diffusion networks), and empirical exponents of 0.63 to 1.20 across three equations decompose into one half plus a measurable angular term. For Burgers' equation, a single-model test based on a block-bootstrap standard error flagged 3 of 300 correctly specified networks (observed false-alarm rate 1%), all 2% misspecifications at a practical budget, and two thirds of 1% misspecifications after convergence. For the self-similar blowup rate of the C\'ordoba-C\'ordoba-Fontelos equation, where the rate also enters the architecture, the estimator recovers about half of the misspecification, whereas $\rho$ increases approximately quadratically and distinguishes a 0.2% error. When the incorrect rate enters both the equation and the architecture, errors of up to 2% were not detected at the precision reached. At practical budgets, the raw loss can be lower for the misspecified model, a scaling effect that $\rho$ does not share.
papers.title_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワークにおけるパラメータ誤指定：閉形式監査とその限界
papers.summary_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）において、学習済みモデルから物理方程式のパラメータ誤指定を検出する手法を提案する。残差がパラメータに対して線形の場合、再学習なしで最小二乗法による推定値を閉形式で導出可能である。この推定の精度は正規化残差ρと相関し、Burgers方程式やCórdoba-Córdoba-Fontelos方程式での検証により、誤指定検出の限界とスケーリング効果の存在が示された。

papers.title: Certified neural approximations for parabolic obstacle problems
papers.summary: Residual-trained neural surrogates carry no error guarantee, a limitation for free-boundary problems such as phase change and contact. We derive guaranteed error bounds for neural approximations of parabolic obstacle problems in first-order state--flux--multiplier form. The main result bounds the flux error of the network and the energy error of its feasible projection $\max\{v,g\}$ by the constitutive residual, the initial mismatch, the complementarity defect, and the PDE residual weighted by $c_F^2/\alpha$, without the coercivity and norm-equivalence constants of the first-order formulation. It extends the Apushkinskaya--Repin majorant for the heat operator to general coefficients, free multipliers and a flux bound. A penetration-consistency result shows that neural triples with arbitrarily small bound exist. Outward-rounded cellwise Taylor-model enclosures turn the bound into a finite computation valid on any adaptive partition. The flux and gradient errors of the projected output are certified below $0.27$ and $0.33$ of the solution scale for a one-dimensional Stefan problem and, after adaptive refinement, below one half for all three trained networks on a two-dimensional expanding disk. On an expanding ellipse the gradient bound stays above one half; substitution diagnostics trace the floor of the trained networks to the projected state near the free boundary, and the remaining gap to enclosure overhead. Without a closed-form solution, a validated lower bound replaces the solution norm; there the enclosure is nearly exact, but the trained networks have errors above the solution scale and no useful accuracy is certified. The bounds control a state--flux norm, not the multiplier or the free-boundary location.

papers.title: Permafrost augmented simulation and forecast using hybrid modeling through spectral neural networks
papers.summary: Purpose - Global warming is impacting several crucial Earth systems, including the permafrost. This study investigates the possibility of performing fast and reliable simulation and forecasting of permafrost behavior, addressing a critical gap in the existing literature related to high computation times and energy costs of the simulations. Methodology - A numerical cryohydrogeological study on water and energy transfer in a forested, continuous permafrost site has been conducted using parallel high-performance computing to simulate the permafrost dynamics. The numerical results reasonably replicate the measured soil temperature profiles and the dynamics of infiltrated waters. This work uses a spectral network to achieve a fast, reliable, and stable surrogate model for the simulations to forecast over long periods of time. The surrogate is also enhanced by assimilating experimental data through the development of a hybrid modeling framework. Findings - The proposed approach improves the physical simulation while maintaining the stability of the dynamic model over long periods of time. The results reveal that the proposed hybrid modeling remains stable in integration and forecasting. The final hybrid solution demonstrates a significant improvement in simulation accuracy when tested against a test set of measurements. Predictions of the permafrost behavior in the coming decade are later made based on the CMIP6 climate change scenarios. Originality - This research offers a novel perspective on permafrost modeling that extends the current understanding of its behavior under different climate change scenarios. It shows a higher-than-expected temperature increase of the permafrost. Moreover, the stable forecasting of climate change effects is demonstrated.

papers.title: Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator with Multi-scale Coupling for Meteorological Downscaling
papers.summary: Meteorological downscaling is crucial for high-resolution regional climate forecasting and disaster early warning. While neural operators have emerged as a promising paradigm for modeling complex spatiotemporal mappings, existing frameworks often struggle with spherical manifold geometric distortions, inherent atmospheric multi-scale coupling mismatches, and lack of explicit atmospheric laws. We propose the Spherical Physics-informed Neural Operator, which utilizes a Spherical Laplacian Decomposition to partition atmospheric fields into hierarchical frequency components, maintaining exact point-wise correspondence across scales. To evaluate these representations at arbitrary locations, we introduce a localized spherical integral operator that approximates continuous kernel transforms via geometry-aware attention. Dynamical consistency is further enforced by embedding differentiable constraints into the learning process. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework attains superior accuracy and zero-shot generalization across various meteorological variables and unseen queries, representing a robust and interpretable solution for global-to-regional meteorological downscaling.

papers.title: Multifidelity Monte Carlo Estimator for High-Dimensional Quantities of Interest
papers.summary: Multifidelity Monte Carlo (MFMC) reduces the cost of estimating the statistics of quantities of interest (QoIs) computed via expensive high-fidelity model by using cheaper low-fidelity models as control variates. We extend MFMC to vector-valued QoIs by replacing the scalar control-variate coefficients with matrices and minimizing a weighted mean-squared error. The optimal full-matrix coefficients are available in closed form, and their variance reduction is summarized by an effective correlation that takes the place of the squared Pearson correlation in the closed-form MFMC design. Restricting the coefficients to block-diagonal, diagonal, and scalar classes gives a nested hierarchy of estimators with increasing variance reduction and increasing pilot-data demand, with closed-form coefficients for compatible weightings. For a scalar QoI obtained by linearly projecting the state, correcting the full state before projecting is never worse at the population level. Experiments on a Gaussian problem, a reduced-order model of an advection--diffusion problem, and a coarse-grid two-phase flow problem show that the best class depends on the pilot size relative to the number of covariance quantities it must estimate, and that reusing the pilot samples lowers the mean-squared error.

papers.title: Steered Not Stirred: Effective Reward Tilting using Surrogate Reward Mixing
papers.summary: Continuous-time generative models, from diffusion models, flow matching, and now flow maps, owe their practical value to high-fidelity generation and steerability. In many applications, a ground-truth latent ``oracle'' reward $R^*$ is unavailable or expensive to evaluate, e.g., human judgments or experimental measurements. Although the oracle reward is not directly observable, it can often be approximated through multiple cheaper surrogates that, individually, provide incomplete characterizations but collectively reveal substantial information about the downstream task. In this paper, we present a method for composing such surrogates to steer a pretrained model toward the distribution tilted by an unavailable $R^*$. Given a small feedback set of oracle rankings or numerical rewards, we introduce Mixing And Reward Tilting for INference-time Improvement (MARTINI), which learns a surrogate composition for plug-and-play use with standard inference-time steering methods. Our theory characterizes surrogate information limits and relates population recovery error to ideal-target KL at small tilt strength. For preferences, the bound additionally accounts for an irreducible mismatch between the Plackett-Luce population target and the conditional mean. Experiments demonstrate improved oracle-tilt fidelity in language generation and ImageNet alignment, and improved joint pose accuracy and validity in protein-ligand cofolding, without inference-time oracle queries.

papers.title: Statistical Learning Theory for Direct Preference Optimization
papers.summary: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) learns from pairwise preferences through a logistic objective whose score-difference parameterization follows the Bradley--Terry model. We study how failure of this modeling assumption limits DPO, distinguishing structural misspecification from limited model capacity and finite-sample estimation. Our main contribution is a characterization of structural approximation error through the triangle-curl of the preference log-odds, which vanishes exactly when preferences admit a Bradley--Terry representation. We upper bound the achievable excess logistic risk by a score-class approximation term and a triangle-curl term, and establish a lower bound proportional to triangle-curl under additional boundedness assumptions. For ReLU score models, including clipped models, we derive explicit approximation rates showing that increasing capacity can eliminate the score-approximation term while leaving the structural obstruction unchanged. We further establish finite-sample bounds for clipped empirical risk minimizers that separate network approximation, structural misspecification, and estimation error. We place these results within a surrogate-risk framework by identifying contextual preference accuracy (CPA) as a natural measure of agreement between preference judgments and changes in pairwise probability ratios relative to the reference policy. Standard logistic consistency and calibration results connect DPO's objective to this policy property and transfer our excess-risk upper bounds to CPA, without treating CPA as a complete measure of generated-response quality.

papers.title: CIS-Transolver: A Cross-Layer Incremental-State Neural Operator for Fine-Scale Automotive Aerodynamic Flow Prediction
papers.summary: Neural operators offer an efficient data-driven approach to rapid prediction of complex automotive aerodynamic flows. However, spectral bias and other factors limit accurate reconstruction of fine-scale flow variations near complex geometries. Existing studies improve the representation and fitting of fine-scale information mainly through information extraction and training objectives. Further study is needed to determine how extracted local details can be used continually in subsequent operator computations and contribute effectively to the overall flow-field representation. We propose CIS-Transolver, a cross-layer incremental-state neural operator that extends fine-scale modeling from local information extraction to its use across layers. The method extracts fine-scale information through local multiscale analysis and encodes it as geometric moment states that are propagated and updated across layers. By combining information from previous layers with feedback to the value representations in Physics-Attention, the method allows local details to contribute continually to subsequent modeling of global physical correlations. We systematically evaluate CIS-Transolver on three public automotive aerodynamics benchmarks, ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML, and DrivAerNet++, covering surface pressure fields and volumetric pressure and velocity fields. CIS-Transolver achieves the lowest mean relative L2 error among the evaluated methods for all five prediction metrics across the three benchmarks. The relative error reductions average 8.72% across the five metrics compared with the best baseline for each metric, reaching 16.38% for ShapeNet-Car pressure prediction and 15.60% for AhmedML velocity prediction. These results provide a new approach to fine-scale flow prediction for complex geometries.

papers.title: PhyPro-FM: A Physics and Prompt-Guided Graph Foundation Model for Contingency Analysis
papers.summary: The continuous evolution of next-generation power systems, characterized by the high penetration of renewable energy resources and dynamic topology variations, poses formidable challenges to traditional N-1/N-2 contingency analysis in terms of computational efficiency and scalability. While deep learning-based methods offer accelerated inference, existing studies predominantly treat contingency analysis as a pure regression problem, often overlooking the physical essence of grid operation and engineering requirements of real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a physics and prompt-guided graph foundation model (PhyPro-FM) for generalizable and engineering-viable contingency analysis. The proposed architecture integrates graph neural networks with a learnable global query mechanism and, notably, introduces a prompt-guided learning paradigm. By leveraging historical snapshots as few-shot prompts, the model dynamically captures correlations between target and historical operating conditions, significantly enhancing generalization capabilities under unseen topologies. Furthermore, we design a physics-informed training mechanism that prioritizes branch power flow errors over nodal voltage errors, aligning the optimization objective with critical grid security constraints. To ensure engineering applicability, a physics-informed inference mechanism is also developed, incorporating a residual-based correction module and a specialized post-processing strategy for singular branches to circumvent numerical instability. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that PhyPro-FM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy and generalization, validating its superior physical consistency and robustness for practical engineering applications.

papers.title: A Simple and General Approach to top-$k$ Selection
papers.summary: This paper considers the Bayesian top-$k$ identification problem, wherein a decision maker is tasked with selecting $k$ items from a pool of items of unknown quality. To assess the items, the decision maker adaptively allocates a fixed sampling budget, where each sample of an item yields a noisy observation of its quality, with the objective of minimizing the expected opportunity cost of the selected set. We propose an approach that allocates each batch of samples by minimizing a surrogate objective derived from an upper bound on the expected opportunity cost. The approach is general: samples can be allocated in batches, the selection size $k$ is arbitrary, and it applies to many sampling distributions. It is also simple and intuitive. We prove that the method's posterior expected opportunity cost decays at an exponential rate of at least half the best rate achievable by any sampling rule. In simulations across a wide range of settings, the method is competitive with, and often improves upon, the best existing algorithm in each setting.

papers.title: A mixed leading variable physics-informed neural network for nonsmooth dynamics simulation in contact systems
papers.summary: High-accuracy computation of nonsmooth dynamics is a challenging problem in systems with multiple frictional contacts. This study proposes a general physics-informed neural network framework, termed the mixed leading variable physics-informed neural network (MLV-PINN). By using the governing equations and contact-friction laws as physical constraints, this framework provides common solution approaches for computing nonsmooth dynamics not only in discrete systems but also in continuum systems. Specifically, the network represents accelerations, normal contact forces and friction margins as independent outputs and determines them simultaneously, without first reducing the dynamics to discrete velocity-impulse complementary subproblems. A composite physics-informed loss is constructed from the equations of motion in their original form, contact-friction complementary conditions and a friction-margin consistency relation. To improve stick-slip state identification during PINN optimisation, a mixed leading variable combining relative tangential velocity and acceleration is introduced to reformulate the tangential complementary conditions. Four benchmark simulations cover one-dimensional (1-D) nonsmooth dynamics involving single-contact stick-slip, 1-D nonsmooth dynamics involving multi-contact stick-slip, two-dimensional (2-D) nonsmooth dynamics with coupled normal contact-separation and tangential stick-slip, and 2-D nonsmooth dynamics in a continuum system involving moving contact on an elastic beam. Benchmark comparisons show substantial reductions in displacement and velocity errors relative to the corresponding conventional methods at large time steps. These results, together with an ablation study and tests involving friction-velocity slopes, long-time integration and loss weights, illustrate the computational accuracy and support the broad applicability of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Sequence-to-Sequence Neural Surrogate Modeling of Transient Responses in High-Speed Links with Variable Design Parameters
papers.summary: This paper presents sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) neural surrogates for high-speed transient response modeling and signal integrity analysis in fixed and variable design parameter spaces. To identify the structural requirements for prediction accuracy, multiple neural architectures were evaluated with respect to different training strategies such as sample-based and unit interval-based, as well as input configurations such as TX-only and TX+RX. For fixed design parameters, feedforward neural networks achieve accuracy comparable to recurrent models while requiring lower computational cost, as the static mapping can be approximated by fully connected and non-sequential representations. Variable design parameters alter the electromagnetic characteristics of the interconnect, which creates parameter-dependent temporal dynamics that require sequence-aware architectures to resolve the evolving interactions within the transient response. The results based on a 14-dimensional variable design parameter scenario show that while autoregressive TX+RX feedback suffers from severe phase drift and error propagation under variable conditions, non-autoregressive TX-only inference leads to stability. To overcome the structural limitations of standard decoders, a recurrent Early Fusion LSTM is proposed, which injects design parameters at the initial encoding stage. This approach achieves superior prediction accuracy, with an RMSE of 31.0 mV and an R2 of 99.51% for transient waveform prediction, an RMSE of 30.7 mV and an R2 of 99.57% for eye-height prediction, and an RMSE of 19.5 ps and an R2 of 99.94% for eye-width prediction. These results demonstrate that neural seq2seq surrogates are accurate for transient response modeling and signal integrity analysis in complex variable design parameter spaces.

papers.title: Beyond Leaderboards: A Method for Application-Specific Capability Profiling of Large Language Models
papers.summary: Public leaderboards rank large language models (LLMs) in general, but an engineer has to choose a model for a specific application, architecture and cost. This paper presents a method for application-specific capability profiling of LLMs and its realization as a containerized testbed. The method treats each application as a unit of extension: an Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration agent, a documentation-grounded chatbot or an enterprise-support automation agent runs in its own container behind a small contract, brings its own dataset, evaluator and owned attributes, and is onboarded together with its dashboards. Measurements accumulate in a versioned, sparse metamodel of every model. The method separates the model under test from judges and agents, freezes and hashes plans, refuses to compare values from different contexts, diagnoses the instrument before the system, and applies a null-agent check and a noise rule whose operating characteristics are quantified by simulation. In the evaluated automation conditions, model choices produced larger differences on selected observable outcomes than framework choices, although the experimental design does not establish a general causal ranking of these factors. The experiments also show that instruction tuning is deployment-specific and that system-reported success can exceed independently observed success: of 216 migration units checked against a real Oracle database, 108 were demonstrably correct. These measurements establish application-specific observations, not a universal model ranking.
papers.title_ja: リーダーボードを超えて：大規模言語モデルのアプリケーション固有の能力プロファイリング手法
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、汎用的なリーダーボードではなく、特定のアプリケーションやコスト制約に基づいてLLMを評価する手法を提案する。コンテナ化されたテストベッドを用い、各アプリケーション固有のデータセットや評価指標を統合し、モデルの能力をバージョン管理されたメタモデルとして蓄積する。実験では、フレームワークの選択よりもモデルの選択が結果に与える影響が大きいことを示し、またシステム報告の成功と独立した観察の成功に乖離があることを明らかにした。この手法は、実務的なデプロイメント環境におけるLLMの選定と評価を支援するものである。

papers.title: Lifting Safety Through Reduced-Order Model Architectures: An Invariant Manifold Approach
papers.summary: Reduced-order model architectures are often used to decompose complex safety-critical control design tasks into tractable subproblems. In this paradigm, one must ask: when does the safety of a reduced-order model lift to safety of the full system? Taking an invariant manifold perspective, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of smooth, regular lifts of compact safe sets from reduced-order models. Our characterization relies only on asymptotic stability of an embedding of a reduced-order safe set, without additional robustness or rate conditions. We apply these results to study control barrier functions in reduced-order model architectures and lifts of safe sets through cascades. Further, we use our conditions to obtain topological obstructions to the tracking of safe, kinematic reduced-order models for mechanical systems. We conclude by using these obstructions to inform safe hierarchical control design for an underactuated satellite on SE(3).
papers.title_ja: 縮約モデルアーキテクチャによる安全性の向上：不変多様体アプローチ
papers.summary_ja: 縮約モデルを用いた安全クリティカルな制御設計において、縮約モデルの安全性が全システムにどのように拡張されるかの必要十分条件を、不変多様体の視点から提示する。制御バリア関数やカスケード構造における安全集合の挙動を分析し、機械系における安全な運動学モデル追従の位相的障害を特定する。最後に、これらの結果を用いて、SE(3)上の非完全駆動衛星に対する安全な階層型制御設計に応用する。

papers.title: Physics-Informed Koopman Learning for Data-Efficient System Identification of Automated Vehicle Dynamics
papers.summary: Understanding how a particular automated vehicle reacts to nearby traffic can improve motion prediction, control development, traffic simulation, and safety evaluation. However, commercial automated driving systems are proprietary, and single encounters may provide only a few seconds of noisy data. Standard physical models are interpretable but inflexible, whereas neural models are often data-hungry. We propose a physics-informed Koopman framework that combines a calibrated car-following law with a correction learned from the observations. A weak-form estimator learns this correction from velocity measurements integrated over time, avoiding noise-sensitive numerical differentiation. The resulting continuous-time model predicts the follower's response and provides interpretable measures of driving behavior. Experiments on OpenACC and CATS-CF evaluate 5-, 7-, and 11-second histories. Averaged over these histories, the constant-time-headway branch reduces speed prediction error by 16.0% and 15.4% on OpenACC and CATS-CF, respectively, relative to the best neural baselines. The PI-Koopman branches achieve the lowest mean speed and gap errors among the physical and neural comparators. Weak-form estimation reduces acceleration-field reconstruction error by 74.5% in noisy known-law simulations and noise-induced field perturbation by 91.6% in paired real-vehicle measurements. The same PI-Koopman system identification supports following-mode recognition with an approximately eleven-fold difference in median residual variance between human drivers and automated vehicles, and a single residual threshold achieves 85.4% balanced accuracy. The branch informed by the intelligent driver model takes a median 17 to 26 ms for identification and forecasting on the tested central processing units, supporting frequent target adaptation.
papers.title_ja: 自動運転車両ダイナミクスのデータ効率の良いシステム同定のための物理情報付きKoopman学習
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、物理法則とデータ駆動型補正を組み合わせる物理情報付きKoopmanフレームワークを提案する。ノイズに弱い数値微分を回避するため、時間積分された速度測定値から弱形式推定器を用いて補正項を学習する。実験では、既存のニューラルベースラインと比較し、速度予測誤差を最大16%低減し、加速度場の再構成誤差を74.5%削減した。さらに、同定と予測をCPU上で17〜26msで実行可能であり、リアルタイムな目標適応やモード認識に応用できることを示した。

papers.title: Self-Supervised In-Context Operator Learning for Optimal Mixing in Incompressible Flows
papers.summary: We develop a self-supervised operator-learning framework for optimal mixing in incompressible flows, aimed at overcoming the computational limitations of classical PDE-constrained optimal control. The objective is to design velocity fields that efficiently homogenize a passive scalar while minimizing kinetic energy, quantified through the $\dot H^{-1}(\Omega)$ mix-norm. Classical methods solve a separate optimal control problem for each initial condition using iterative forward-adjoint procedures, leading to substantial computational costs and limited scalability. In contrast, we propose to learn the solution operator that maps initial scalar fields to optimal mixing controls directly. The proposed self-supervised method does not require access to supervised labels, thereby significantly reducing the data-generation burden of supervised operator-learning methods. Our framework integrates a Lagrangian reformulation of the transport equation with a transformer-based neural operator architecture. The transport dynamics are represented through characteristic ODEs, enabling particle-based Monte Carlo optimization, while the learned velocity field is parameterized in a divergence-free spectral basis enforcing incompressibility and no-penetration conditions exactly. Numerical experiments on parametric families of initial conditions in two and three spatial dimensions demonstrate robust generalization to unseen regimes and approximately exponential decay of the mix-norm. The learned controls also transfer consistently to independent Eulerian finite-volume simulations, validating the physical fidelity of the learned operator. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first self-supervised operator-learning framework for optimal mixing and among the first data-driven approaches for optimal mixing in fully three-dimensional incompressible flows.
papers.title_ja: 非圧縮流における最適混合のための自己教師ありインコンテキストオペレータ学習
papers.summary_ja: 非圧縮流における最適混合問題に対し、古典的なPDE制約最適化の計算コストを削減する自己教師ありオペレータ学習フレームワークを提案する。ラグランジュ再定式化とTransformerベースのニューラルオペレータを統合し、初期スカラー場から最適制御へ直接マッピングする解演算子进行学习する。教師データ不要であり、2次元・3次元の数値実験で未知の初期条件への汎化性能と、独立した有限体積法シミュレーションへの転移可能性を実証した。

papers.title: Composable Parametric Demographic Injection for Values Survey Simulation
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as simulated respondents in computational social science, yet accurately reproducing population-specific heterogeneous response distributions remains challenging. Existing methods such as demographic prompting are sensitive to prompt design and increase inference overhead, while parameter-based methods struggle to reuse demographic information efficiently, limiting generalization to unseen combinations. In this regard, we propose PARADE, a composable PARAmetric DEmographic injection framework that represents each demographic attribute value with a reusable and composable LoRA module. Specifically, PARADE separates task-common survey capability from demographic-specific value shifts via a shared Task LoRA and attribute-level Demographic LoRAs, with composition calibration to reduce parameter interference. At inference time, target population models can be constructed on demand by recombining the relevant modules, including demographic combinations not observed during training. Extensive experiments on the World Values Survey and SocioBench across three backbone models show that PARADE achieves strong population-level distribution alignment while maintaining competitive predictive performance, reducing KL divergence by up to 52.8% relative to the strongest baseline.
papers.title_ja: 価値観調査シミュレーションのための組み合わせ可能なパラメトリックな人口統計情報注入
papers.summary_ja: LLMを用いた社会科学的な調査シミュレーションにおいて、人口統計属性に応じた回答分布を正確に再現する手法PARADEを提案する。各属性値を再利用可能なLoRAモジュールとして表現し、タスク共通能力と属性固有のシフトを分離することで、学習時に観測されなかった属性の組み合わせも推論時に柔軟に構築可能にする。World Values Survey等の実験により、既存手法と比較してKLダイバージェンスを最大52.8%低減し、集団レベルの分布適合性を向上させることを示した。

papers.title: Zero-Shot Tabular Learning via Hypergraph Reasoning with LLMs
papers.summary: Tabular data are prevalent across diverse domains such as healthcare and finance. Zero-shot tabular learning aims to make predictions without labeled data. However, existing LLM-based approaches rely on row-wise prompting, resulting in high inference cost and limited use of inter-row dependencies. In this work, we propose TABHGR+, an efficient relation-aware zero-shot framework for tabular data that leverages LLM-generated rules to label and group rows. Specifically, based on column and task descriptions, we use LLMs to generate rules that assign weak labels to all rows. To refine these noisy weak labels, we construct a hypergraph by grouping semantically related rows using LLM-generated rules and perform hypergraph-based label propagation. Lastly, we further enhance the LLM-generated hypergraph for propagation, which is potentially sub-optimal, by assigning label-adaptive weights to hyperedges. By requiring only a constant number of LLM calls independent of dataset size, TABHGR+ substantially reduces inference cost while achieving higher classification accuracy than zero-shot and strong few-shot baselines.
papers.title_ja: LLMを用いたハイパーグラフ推論によるゼロショット表形式データ学習
papers.summary_ja: 表形式データにおけるゼロショット学習の推論コスト削減と精度向上を目的としたフレームワークTABHGR+を提案する。LLMで生成されたルールを用いて行をグループ化し、ハイパーグラフ構造を構築することで、行間の依存関係を効率的に活用する。ラベル伝播とハイパーエッジへの重み付けにより、データサイズに依存しない定数のLLM呼び出し回数で、既存のゼロショットやフェューショットベースラインを上回る分類精度を実現した。

papers.title: Organizing LLM Inference for Aggregate Predictions from Behavioral Data
papers.summary: When using a large language model (LLM) to simulate a user population, how should we combine individual behavioral histories to predict the fraction of users who take a particular action? We study this question in e-commerce, predicting observed product-level conversion rates from browsing sessions without task-specific model training. We vary two design choices, each involving a bias-variance tradeoff. Summarizing a product's sessions before inference reduces cost but can discard predictive detail, adding bias, whereas predicting outcomes for individual sessions and averaging afterward preserves that detail but requires many calls to reduce variance. Evaluating products together in one prompt can help the model infer what is typical in the setting, reducing bias, but also makes each prediction depend on which other products appear alongside it, adding noise. We evaluate both choices across five LLMs and two datasets. Our main finding is that predictions from individual sessions outperform predictions from summaries when products are evaluated separately, but summaries lead when products are evaluated together. Comparative summaries achieve the highest Spearman correlation with observed rates in 12 of 15 settings, with no alternative significantly better. Comparison thus helps summaries far more than session predictions, overcoming the advantage of behavioral detail. We interpret this difference through a Bayesian model of the second tradeoff, which suggests that comparison helps more when the inputs in a prompt reveal more about differences across products, consistent with our results for four types of comparative context. Comparative summaries also incur a small fraction of the inference cost of the session methods. With the best model for each outcome, they attain 66-89% of the correlation of the best supervised benchmark trained on thousands of labeled products.
papers.title_ja: 行動データからの集計予測のためのLLM推論の組織化
papers.summary_ja: ECサイトにおける商品別コンバージョン率予測において、LLMを用いた推論時の入力設計（個別セッション予測 vs 要約予測、個別評価 vs 比較評価）の影響を分析した。バイアスと分散のトレードオフを考慮し、5つのLLMと2つのデータセットで評価した結果、比較的要約を用いた手法が最も高い相関を示した。この手法は、個別セッション予測に比べて推論コストを大幅に削減しつつ、教師ありモデルの66〜89%の性能を達成する。ベイジアンモデルによる解釈を通じて、比較コンテキストが予測精度向上に寄与するメカニズムを説明している。
