papers.title: Beyond Prediction: A Component-Level Study of Concept Recovery in In-Context Learning
papers.summary: In-context learning (ICL) enables language models to make accurate predictions from demonstrations, but prediction success alone does not reveal the extent to which the underlying concept has been recovered. Existing evaluations typically assess recovery at the level of the whole concept, making it difficult to identify which components are recovered and to separate model limitations from ambiguity in the demonstrations. We introduce a component-level framework for concept recovery that decomposes concepts into their defining components and uses controlled structural interventions to evaluate both component-level and whole-concept recovery under identifiable demonstrations. Across four instruction-tuned LLMs and three composition forms, we find that models often achieve high prediction accuracy despite poor whole-concept recovery, with systematic over-specification of relevant attributes and level constraints. Individual structural components are generally insufficient for whole-concept recovery, whereas jointly specifying complementary components, particularly relevant attributes and their level constraints, substantially improves recovery. However, this improvement is fragile: a single plausible but unnecessary level constraint can substantially disrupt recovery. Finally, joint supervision of recovery and implicit prediction substantially improves recovery while preserving prediction performance, with the learned capability transferring across composition forms. Overall, our component-level analysis provides a more diagnostic view of what models recover from demonstrations than the existing holistic view.
papers.title_ja: 予測を超えて：インコンテキスト学習における概念回復のコンポーネントレベル研究
papers.summary_ja: インコンテキスト学習（ICL）において、予測精度が高くても背後にある概念が正しく回復されていない場合がある問題に対し、概念を構成要素に分解して評価するフレームワークを提案する。4つのLLMを用いた実験では、予測精度が高いにもかかわらず概念全体の回復率が低く、属性やレベル制約の過剰指定が起きていることが判明した。補完的な構成要素を同時に指定することで回復率は向上するが、不要な制約一つで大きく崩壊する脆弱性も確認された。回復と予測の共同学習により、構成形式を跨いで汎用性のある概念回復能力を獲得できることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの内部メカニズム解明と評価手法の改善に直結する

papers.title: ReTTT: Reflection-Driven Test-Time Training via Experience-Based Parametric Memory
papers.summary: LLM agents accumulate valuable task-specific information through their actions, observations, and environmental feedback during multi-turn task execution. When effectively used, this information can help agents refine subsequent decisions and improve task performance. However, the learning value of an interaction depends on its context and subsequent feedback, making it challenging to extract reliable, actionable lessons and revise them as the task unfolds. In this paper, we introduce ReTTT, which enables experience-driven self-adaptation through test-time training on lessons constructed and continually revised within an episode. ReTTT lets the agent reflect on interaction feedback, maintain the resulting lessons in an explicit memory, and learn from them by updating an episode-local LoRA adapter while keeping the backbone frozen. The adapted model then performs both subsequent actions and reflection, coupling policy adaptation with the construction of future learning experience. We evaluate ReTTT on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and SWE-bench Lite using two model families. ReTTT outperforms trajectory-based test-time training across all six model--benchmark settings, improving task success by up to 12.14 percentage points. A frozen-reflection comparison further shows a 7.14-point benefit from adapting the reflection policy, while trajectory analysis illustrates how adapted reflection derives more task-specific guidance from failed attempts. These findings suggest that learning to reflect on its own behavior can boost agents' performance on long-horizon tasks.
papers.title_ja: ReTTT: 経験ベースのパラメトリックメモリを用いた反復駆動型テスト時学習
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントがマルチターンタスク実行中に得た経験から、エピソード内で教訓を構築・修正し、テスト時学習を通じて自己適応を行う手法ReTTTを提案する。バックボーンを凍結したまま、エピソードローカルなLoRAアダプタを更新することで、行動と反射（リフレクション）の両方を改善する。ALFWorld、ScienceWorld、SWE-bench Liteでの評価により、従来の軌道ベースのテスト時学習を上回る性能（最大12.14ポイント向上）を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計と推論時の適応手法であり、ユーザーの関心領域に直結する。

papers.title: Compaction-Aware Reinforcement Learning For Ascend Triton Kernel Generation
papers.summary: Automatically generating high-performance kernels with LLM-based agents promises substantial gains in development efficiency, but two obstacles remain. First, while increasing multi-turn interaction with execution environments is crucial for refining generation quality, continuous context accumulation rapidly exceeds the model's effective context window. Second, training long-horizon tasks via GRPO inherently incurs sparse rewards due to its reliance on terminal outcome evaluation, severely hindering step-level credit assignment; To address these obstacles, we propose ATRL (Ascend Triton Reinforcement Learning), a post-training method that refines GRPO into a compaction-aware, segment-level objective for long-horizon kernel generation. We also design a lightweight agent harness providing cascaded compilation, correctness, and profiling feedback, alongside an Ascend-specific knowledge base injected during agentic RL training and evaluation to compensate for the base model's missing platform expertise. Evaluations on NPUKernelBench and KernelBench, both executed on Ascend hardware, show that ATRL consistently surpasses all baselines, including GRPO, in both correctness and speedup.
papers.title_ja: Ascend Triton カーネル生成のための圧縮認識型強化学習
papers.summary_ja: LLMエージェントによる高性能カーネル自動生成において、コンテキストウィンドウの超過と報酬のスパース化という課題を解決する手法「ATRL」を提案する。GRPOを改良し、長期的なタスクにおけるセグメントレベルの目標関数と、コンテキスト圧縮を考慮した設計を採用している。さらに、Ascendハードウェア向けの知識ベースを注入し、コンパイル・正解性・プロファイリングのフィードバックを段階的に提供する軽量エージェントハーネスを構築した。NPUKernelBenchおよびKernelBenchでの評価により、既存手法を上回る正解率と高速化性能を実証した。

papers.title: UltraData-Code: From Raw Repositories to Algorithmically Dense and Task-Oriented Code Data
papers.summary: Code generation has become a core capability of large language models (LLMs), and code data is central to the pre-training process that develops it. As obtaining public code of sufficient quality becomes more difficult, further progress cannot rely on corpus expansion alone. Tiered data management instead applies increasingly targeted processing to smaller data pools, producing data states suited to different training objectives. Following this perspective, we present UltraData-Code as four connected data states spanning repository archival at L0, standardized natural code at L1, algorithmic selection at L2, and task-oriented synthesis at L3. L0 preserves repository data and provenance for reprocessing, while L1 applies scalable filtering, normalization, and near-deduplication for broad pre-training. L2 selects high-quality algorithmically relevant files using language-adaptive relevance signals and quality constraints, yielding approximately 400B tokens of UltraData-Code-L2 across 11 programming languages for focused continual pre-training. L3 converts selected implementations into structured programming exercises, yielding approximately 150B tokens of UltraData-Code-L3 across the same 11 languages for task-oriented mid-training or supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Under controlled 10B-token continual pre-training of a 1B model, L2 improves pass@1 over L1 by 7.80 percentage points (pp) on EvalPlus and 5.13pp on MultiPL-E. Replacing half of the L2 training tokens with L3 yields a further gain of 8.42pp and 8.07pp on the two benchmarks, respectively. Both gains increase when the training budget scales to 100B tokens. We have released our datasets and classifiers to support further research on LLMs.
papers.title_ja: UltraData-Code: 生リポジトリからアルゴリズム的に高密度でタスク指向のコードデータへ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、大規模言語モデル（LLM）のコード生成能力向上を目的とした階層的なデータ管理手法「UltraData-Code」を提案する。リポジトリのアーカイブ（L0）から標準化（L1）、アルゴリズム的選別（L2）、タスク指向の合成（L3）までの4段階のデータ状態を定義し、各段階で異なる学習目標に適したデータを生成する。特にL2とL3のデータを用いた継続事前学習やSFTにより、EvalPlusやMultiPL-Eなどのベンチマークで既存手法より大幅な性能向上（最大8.42pp）を実証した。11言語に対応する約400Bトークン（L2）と150Bトークン（L3）のデータセットを公開し、LLMのコード特化型学習におけるデータ品質と効率化の重要性を示している。

papers.title: A Controlled LLM Workflow for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis of Risk Score Differences
papers.summary: We propose a controlled Large Language Model (LLM) workflow for explaining risk score differences using similar historical transactions. The workflow combines reference retrieval and contrastive SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) evidence with reference-based LLM reasoning and deterministic validation. Experiments on a test dataset show that the workflow produces more consistent, evidence-grounded and traceable diagnoses than the same LLM without structured workflow guidance.
papers.title_ja: リスクスコアの差分に対する証拠に基づく診断のための制御されたLLMワークフロー
papers.summary_ja: 類似した過去の取引データを参照し、対照的なSHAP値を用いてリスクスコアの差分を説明するLLMワークフローを提案する。参照検索と決定論的検証を組み合わせたこの手法により、構造化されたガイドなしの場合よりも一貫性が高く、証拠に基づいた追跡可能な診断が可能になることを実験で示した。

papers.title: Do Knowledge and Reasoning Oriented Benchmarks Induce Stable Representation Signatures in LLMs?
papers.summary: Internal signatures could support monitoring, adaptive computation, and mechanistic analysis, but benchmark prompts can be separable without any shared computational distinction. We test whether a prespecified knowledge/reasoning label defines a reusable internal signature in five contemporary 7B to 31B models. We treat the \textbf{task} as the unit of inference probes hold out complete tasks, labels are permuted across tasks, and the best layer and stream are reselected for every permutation. Raw probes recover an eight-versus-eight-subject MMLU partition in all five models (macro-F1 $0.78$--$0.81$), but prompt text predicts it nearly as well: under an identical probe configuration, the activation advantage is only $0.017$--$0.070$ macro-F1 and is not significant. At the prespecified $0.01$ level, lexical adjustment removes significance while the adjusted states still identify individual subjects, and the selected site changes across task panels and selection rules. Additionally, two released base-training trajectories show no common direction. These pooled layerwise measures recover the task label but identify no transferable knowledge/reasoning signature at the tested sensitivity, which cannot exclude moderate effects. The resulting protocol gives future internal monitors and intervention studies a sequence of tests to pass. Project page: \url{https://parsa-ra.github.io/lmbehave/}.
papers.title_ja: 知識と推論に焦点を当てたベンチマークは、LLM内で安定した表現シグネチャを誘発するのか？
papers.summary_ja: 本研究では、大規模言語モデル（LLM）内部の表現が「知識」と「推論」のタスク間で安定したシグネチャを持つかを検証した。5つのモデルを用いた解析の結果、タスクラベルは復元可能だが、それはプロンプトのテキスト情報だけでほぼ説明がつき、モデル内部の計算的差異によるものではないことが示された。また、層やストリームの選択ルールによって結果が変動し、汎用性のある内部シグネチャは存在しないことが判明した。このプロトコルは、将来の内部監視や介入研究のための厳密な評価基準を提供する。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの内部表現解析とベンチマーク評価手法に深く関連

papers.title: Visual Causal-chain Bookmarking: Retrieval-Weighted Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Reward
papers.summary: RL agents trained on a single trajectory-level return face a credit-assignment problem: when a reward arrives many steps after the decision that caused it, every action gets the same signal regardless of causal responsibility. This paper studies Visual Causal-chain Bookmarking (VCBM), which concentrates credit on the decision points that determine an episode's return, via two instantiations. The first targets a fully observed, low-dimensional MDP (a delayed-reward watch-repair task), where VCBM statistically discovers which state components the agent causally controls and estimates per-decision-point action values directly, evaluated against ground truth and RUDDER, an LSTM-based baseline. VCBM converges to 95.07% correct decisions in a mean of 1,532.3 episodes across 20 seeds, versus RUDDER's slower, more variable convergence (mean 3,327.1 episodes; p<0.001); VCBM's discovered causal structure exactly matches ground truth in all seeds. The second targets a partially observed, language-based setting: an LLM agent trained with Leave-One-Out PPO (LOOP) in AppWorld, where causal discovery is intractable and a structural heuristic (state-mutating tool calls) substitutes for it, with credit distributed via retrieval over episodic memory and blended with LOOP's advantage. Over 200 iterations on identical Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct/LoRA/FSDP2 configurations, VCBM-blended LOOP improves task success over plain LOOP (0.354 vs. 0.458), reduces final-step max importance weight, and improves token efficiency, with a small KL exception favouring LOOP. The watch-repair result supports the claim that weighting causally relevant steps is more sample-efficient than an undifferentiated baseline or a learned return-redistribution network; the AppWorld result, limited to one seed per arm by a 2-GPU budget, is a compute-limited demonstration at a harder, natural-language scale, not a statistical confirmation.
papers.title_ja: 視覚的因果連鎖ブックマーク：遅延報酬からの強化学習における検索重み付きクレジット割り当て
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、遅延報酬環境における強化学習のクレジット割り当て問題を解決する「視覚的因果連鎖ブックマーク（VCBM）」を提案する。低次元MDPでは因果構造を統計的に発見し、LLMエージェントではツール呼び出しなどの構造的特徴を用いて因果的に重要なステップにクレジットを集中させる。実験では、ベースライン手法よりもサンプル効率が高く、LLMエージェントのタスク成功率とトークン効率の向上が示された。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習とLLMエージェント設計の両方に深く関連する手法

papers.title: Prefix-Tuning for Arbitrary Output Sequences on Pretrained Transformers
papers.summary: Prefix-tuning is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for large language models (LLMs) that steers model outputs by prepending task-specific prefix representations to the input sequence. Despite its practical success, the theoretical understanding of the expressiveness of prefixes remains incomplete. In particular, the following question remains open: Given a pretrained autoregressive Transformer, for any input-output sequence pair $(\mathtt{x},\mathtt{y})$, does there always exist a prefix $\mathcal{S}$ such that prepending $\mathcal{S}$ to $\mathtt{x}$ induces the model to generate the target output $\mathtt{y}$? In this work, we prove that under the assumption that $\mathtt{y}$ is in the range of the pretrained Transformer, such a prefix $\mathcal{S}$ exists and can be explicitly computed by solving multiple linear systems. We further show that this assumption is necessary, in the sense that such a prefix may not exist when the assumption fails, thereby providing a complete answer to the above question. Our analysis is constructive and the obtained theoretical results hold under fairly general assumptions on model architecture. Extensive experiments on GPT-2 and Qwen3-4B demonstrate that our algorithm produces prefixes with strong control over model outputs.
papers.title_ja: 事前学習済みトランスフォーマーにおける任意の出力シーケンスのためのプレフィックスチューニング
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、大規模言語モデル（LLM）のパラメータ効率の良いファインチューニング手法であるプレフィックスチューニングの表現力について理論的に分析する。事前学習済みモデルが特定の出力を生成可能である場合、その出力を誘導するプレフィックスが常に存在し、線形方程式系を解くことで明示的に計算可能であることを証明した。また、この条件が満たされない場合、対応するプレフィックスが存在しない可能性を示し、理論的な完全性を確保している。GPT-2やQwen3-4Bを用いた実験により、提案アルゴリズムがモデル出力を強力に制御できることを実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの効率化手法であるプレフィックスチューニングの理論的基盤と実証を含むため

papers.title: Web Agent Agentic Reinforcement Learning Decision Model Under Multi-Cost and Failure Risk
papers.summary: Intelligent agent interactions in real-world web environments are commonly constrained by request budgets, time delays, anti-crawling restrictions, and operational failure risks. Strategies solely optimizing task success rates often exhibit unusable phenomena such as "high success but high cost" or "low risk but conservative failure." This paper proposes a constrained agentic reinforcement learning model for web agents, unifying page access, search requests, and external API calls into a unified long-term decision-making framework with associated costs. It simultaneously incorporates cost budget constraints and tail risk control into the optimization objective: constructing a multidimensional cost vector comprising cumulative request count, total latency, and failure penalties to achieve budget compliance via Lagrange dual updates, while employing a CVaR risk term to suppress excessive exploration of high-failure-probability paths, thereby achieving an adaptive balance among "completion rate, cost, and risk." Experiments were conducted across 30-70 site/page templates and 800-1,500 end-to-end web tasks, including information extraction, price comparison, form submission, and cross-page navigation. Interaction sequences spanned 20-120 steps with tool scales of 30-200. Performance was benchmarked against unconstrained RL, budget-constrained RL, and rule-based/scripted web agents, quantifying task completion rates, cost-per-success, failure rates, and policy stability. Results demonstrate that at equivalent completion rates, our method reduces C-PS by 22%-31% and lowers failure rates by 18%-26% under high failure penalties. Under fixed budgets, task completion rates increase by 10%-16%, highlighting the necessity and effectiveness of constraint modeling for practical web agent deployment.
papers.title_ja: マルチコストと失敗リスク下におけるWebエージェントの強化学習意思決定モデル
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、Web環境におけるエージェントの行動を、コスト予算と失敗リスクを考慮した制約付き強化学習モデルとして定式化する。ページアクセスやAPI呼び出しなどのコストベクトルを統合し、ラグランジュ乗数法による予算制約とCVaRによる尾部リスク制御を最適化目標に組み込むことで、完了率・コスト・リスクのバランスを最適化する。30〜70サイトのテンプレートと800〜1,500件のタスクで検証し、既存手法と比較して同等の完了率でコストを22〜31%削減し、固定予算下では完了率を10〜16%向上させることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計と強化学習の応用であり、実務的なコスト最適化に直結する

papers.title: SAGE-CP: When Marginal Coverage Hides Route-Conditional Failures in Adaptive VLM Ensembles
papers.summary: Adaptive VLM ensembles save computation by stopping early on easy images and escalating harder ones. Although a single conformal threshold can make the final predictor marginally valid, it can still fail severely along individual computational routes. We characterize this failure precisely: if a route has prevalence pi, marginal 1-alpha coverage allows its conditional coverage to fall to max{0, 1-alpha/pi}. To address this mismatch, we learn the router on development data, freeze all routing choices, and calibrate the returned score separately for early exits and escalated inputs. We call this pipeline SAGE-CP. Its calibration step applies Mondrian split conformal prediction to the operational groups created by the router. Under exchangeability, the resulting prediction sets achieve finite-sample coverage within each route. Across 10 benchmarks, 4 frozen VLMs, and 5 aligned splits, both global calibration and SAGE-CP achieve 0.900 marginal coverage at a 0.90 target, but their route behavior differs substantially. SAGE-CP raises mean worst-route coverage from 0.623 to 0.887 and reduces the mean route-coverage gap from 0.324 to 0.025, using the same routed scores and 1.177 source calls per image. The stronger guarantee increases the mean prediction-set size from 1.893 to 2.212; nevertheless, the sets remain smaller than those of the full ensemble (2.486) while requiring 70.6 percent fewer source calls. The route-level reliability persists across 6 fixed query fractions, while finer exit-depth groups demonstrate the need for additional calibration data on rare routes. Across 5 datasets, SAGE-CP also reduces measured batch-one latency by 58.8 to 63.4 percent and gross GPU energy by 55.7 to 57.5 percent relative to full inference. Thus, routing provides computational savings, while route-stratified calibration attaches coverage guarantees to the operational paths created by the router.
papers.title_ja: SAGE-CP: 適応型VLMアンサンブルにおける辺縁カバレッジが経路条件付き失敗を隠蔽する問題
papers.summary_ja: 適応型VLMアンサンブルでは、計算コスト削減のための早期終了ルーティングにより、全体のカバレッジは保証されても個別の計算経路での信頼度が低下する問題がある。本論文は、この経路条件付きカバレッジの劣化を定式化し、Mondrian分割適合予測を用いて各経路ごとにスコアを較正する手法SAGE-CPを提案する。10種のベンチマークで、SAGE-CPは最悪経路のカバレッジを0.623から0.887へ向上させ、予測セットサイズを拡大しつつもフル推論比でGPUエネルギーを約56%削減した。これにより、計算効率と統計的保証の両立を実現する。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論高速化と評価手法の両方に直結する

papers.title: DS-Net: A Dynamic Split Network for Edge-Cloud Collaborative Inference
papers.summary: Collaborative inference serves as a critical methodology in edge intelligence. Existing collaborative inference methods operate by splitting the deep neural network (DNN) model between edge devices and cloud servers. However, these methods need to load different models for multiple split points when the communication or device changes, thus resulting in long switching times and substantial storage overhead on the edge side. To address this issue, we propose a Dynamic Split Network (DS-Net), which not only enables efficient split point switching but also enhances the collaborative speed and accuracy across various scenarios. Specifically, we design a dynamic switching framework that enables flexible selection among multiple split points within a single model, thereby reducing storage, memory, and switching overhead. To mitigate the feature distribution shifts and task-relevant information loss caused by dynamic splitting and high-ratio compression, we further propose a hierarchical compensation mechanism. Local alignment calibrates the decoded feature distribution at each split point, while task-specific global compensation restores task-relevant information at the global level. In addition, we incorporate sample-adaptive global compensation selection into split-point selection based on sample complexity and runtime resource conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that DS-Net reduces memory overhead by 74.6% and achieves millisecond-level switching latency. Moreover, under a 10 Mbps bandwidth constraint on the Nano platform, DS-Net outperforms state-of-the-art collaborative methods by achieving 1.2% higher accuracy on the COCO dataset, reducing latency by 42.5%, and improving throughput by a factor of 1.8$\times$.
papers.title_ja: DS-Net: エッジ・クラウド協調推論のための動的分割ネットワーク
papers.summary_ja: エッジデバイスとクラウドサーバー間の協調推論において、分割点の切り替えに伴うストレージ負荷と遅延を軽減する動的分割ネットワーク（DS-Net）を提案する。単一のモデル内で複数の分割点を柔軟に選択できるフレームワークを設計し、メモリ・スイッチングオーバーヘッドを大幅に削減した。さらに、動的分割や高圧縮率による特徴分布のシフトや情報損失を補正する階層型補償メカニズムを導入し、精度と速度の両立を実現した。実験では、メモリ負荷を74.6%削減し、ミリ秒単位の切り替え遅延と、既存手法を上回る推論性能を達成した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM推論の効率化・エッジ推論・モデル圧縮に直結する手法

papers.title: Learning Whole-Body Kinetic Coordination for Wheeled-Quadruped Long-Range Throwing
papers.summary: Long-range throwing on unstructured terrain is a key capability for mobile robots in delivery and retrieval tasks, but it requires high release velocity, coordinated whole-body motion, and robustness to terrain-induced disturbances. We present a whole-body kinetic-coordination framework for a wheeled-quadruped manipulator that combines kinetic-chain arm modeling with SQP-based trajectory optimization and a reference-guided reinforcement learning policy for coordinated base motion. The manipulator is first reduced to a kinetic-chain model and optimized under kinematic and dynamic constraints to produce a high-speed throwing reference. On a stationary base, the optimized arm trajectory reaches a release speed of 12.75 m/s and a throwing distance of 16.68 m. When whole-body coordination is enabled, the system further increases the release speed to 16.64 m/s and the throwing distance to 28.25 m. We then integrate the mobility of the wheeled-quadruped platform and validate the complete policy through hardware experiments on flat ground, grass, slopes, and rough roads. The results show that kinetic-chain optimization and whole-body coordination together enable robust long-range throwing across diverse unstructured terrains.
papers.title_ja: 車輪付き四脚ロボットの長距離投擲のための全身運動協調学習
papers.summary_ja: 車輪付き四脚マニピュレータにおける長距離投擲能力を高めるための全身運動協調フレームワークを提案する。運動連鎖モデルとSQPベースの軌道最適化により高速な投擲参照軌道を生成し、これに基づいてベースモーションを協調制御する強化学習ポリシーを設計した。静止ベースでは16.68m、全身協調により28.25mの投擲距離を実現し、平坦地や草地、斜面など多様な非構造化地形でのハードウェア実験を通じてその頑健性を検証した。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習と軌道最適化の組み合わせだが、対象がロボットであり軌道力学とは異なる

papers.title: Attitude Estimation of Falcon 9 Rocket Body Based on Photometric Characteristics
papers.summary: The proliferation of space debris, driven by increasingly frequent space activities, poses a severe risk to operational satellites and future missions. Consequently, the surveillance and characterization of space objects have become critical. Current methods for attitude estimation of space objects often rely on target-specific models, such as those with a closed set of facets, and typically employ nonlinear filtering or machine learning techniques. However, these approaches often lack general applicability. This study proposes a more general approach to attitude estimation based on photometric light curves. We define a loss function that quantifies the discrepancy between the measured light curve and a theoretical model parameterized by the attitude parameters. By leveraging automatic differentiation to compute the gradients of this function, we use a gradient descent algorithm to achieve rapid and accurate attitude estimation. The proposed method provides a versatile and efficient framework for attitude estimation, overcoming the target-specificity limitations of existing techniques, with the parameters estimation time reduced to 15 seconds and the mean square error lowered to three decimal places. Validation on the third-party database demonstrates that the method exhibits strong generalization capability.
papers.title_ja: 光度学的特性に基づくファルコン9ロケット本体の姿勢推定
papers.summary_ja: 宇宙デブリの監視において、対象固有のモデルに依存しない汎用的な姿勢推定手法を提案する。光度学的な光曲線と理論モデルの誤差を損失関数として定義し、自動微分を用いた勾配降下法で姿勢パラメータを高速に推定する。この手法により、推定時間は15秒に短縮され、平均二乗誤差も3桁目まで低減された。第三者データベースによる検証で、既存手法に比べ優れた汎化性能を持つことを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 機械学習手法の応用だが、軌道力学やLLMとは直接無関係

papers.title: ATLAS: Expert-Guided Sustainable Satellite Backhaul for Off-Grid Wildlife Monitoring
papers.summary: Remote wildlife monitoring increasingly depends on high-fidelity cameras and sensors deployed far from grid power and terrestrial networks. Low Earth orbit satellite links can provide connectivity in these settings, but their high power draw and variable bandwidth, combined with intermittent on-site solar harvesting, make continuous backhaul infeasible. Current systems therefore filter at the edge, with motion triggers that waste limited energy and bandwidth on environmental artifacts, or fixed vision models that cannot follow evolving expert objectives. We present \textsc{ATLAS}, an expert-guided edge-to-cloud system that treats satellite backhaul as a scarce resource for off-grid wildlife monitoring. \textsc{ATLAS} uses foundation models to compile natural-language expert intent into semantic scoring logic, combines semantic relevance with environmental and energy state, and uses a constrained reinforcement-learning scheduler to decide which clips to upload and when. As a representative case study, we deployed \textsc{ATLAS} for over six months across 18 off-grid salmon-monitoring river sites. \textsc{ATLAS} achieves a mean clip-selection accuracy of $87.4\%$, exceeding mean baseline accuracy by $26.4$ percentage points, while maintaining near-continuous operation through low-solar periods in which baselines incur 16.0\% downtime.
papers.title_ja: ATLAS: 専門家主導によるオフグリッド野生生物監視のための持続可能な衛星バックホール
papers.summary_ja: 電力・通信リソースが限られたオフグリッド環境での野生生物監視向けに、衛星リンクを効率的に活用するエッジからクラウドまでのシステム「ATLAS」を提案する。自然言語で記述された専門家の意図を基盤モデルでセマンティックなスコアリングロジックに変換し、環境状態やエネルギー残量と組み合わせて、アップロードすべき映像クリップとタイミングを決定する。この判断には制約付き強化学習スケジューラを用いる。6ヶ月以上にわたり18箇所のサーモン監視サイトでの実証実験では、クリップ選択精度がベースラインより26.4ポイント向上し、低日照期でもほぼ連続的な運用を実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習とLLM活用が含まれるが、宇宙工学や軌道力学との直接的な関連は薄い。

papers.title: Humanoid SRL: Augmenting Humanoids with Supernumerary Limbs for Coordinated Loco-Manipulation
papers.summary: Humanoid robots are envisioned to perform diverse human-level tasks through their anthropomorphic morphology. Their dual-arm configuration enables a broad range of everyday actions. Yet, as in humans, this morphology can constrain loco-manipulation when both arms are occupied or additional contacts are required beyond their reach. Supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) offer a way to extend these capabilities, but their integration requires the added limb to be coordinated with whole-body motion and balance. In this study, we develop and integrate a supernumerary arm into a humanoid platform to investigate how morphological augmentation reshapes its feasible action space. Through quantitative analysis and hardware experiments across two configurations, we show how the additional limb expands whole-body interaction capabilities by enabling manipulation and support to be coordinated beyond the constraints of the native dual-arm configuration. To control this augmented morphology, we leverage model-based trajectory optimization (TO) to generate dynamically feasible motions for goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (RL) controllers. The controllers are trained in simulation and transferred to hardware in a zero-shot manner, enabling coordinated whole-body skills for contact-rich tri-arm loco-manipulation. We further show vision-guided autonomous execution on selected tasks using diffusion policies trained from hardware demonstrations. Our findings suggest that humanoid morphology need not be restricted to human-like forms, but can be reimagined as an extensible design space for robotic augmentation.
papers.title_ja: ヒューマノイドSRL：協調的な移動操作のためにヒューマノイドに余剰四肢を追加する
papers.summary_ja: ヒューマノイドロボットに余剰な腕（SRL）を追加し、両手が塞がっている場合や到達範囲外の操作・支持を可能にする研究である。モデルベースの軌道最適化（TO）で動的に実行可能な運動を生成し、それを条件付き強化学習（RL）コントローラーの教師データとして利用した。シミュレーションで訓練したコントローラーをハードウェアへゼロショット転移させ、3本腕による接触リッチな移動操作を実現した。さらに、デモデータから訓練した拡散ポリシーを用いたビジョンガイドの自律実行も示している。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習と軌道最適化の活用は関心領域だが、対象が宇宙ではなくロボット制御であるため

papers.title: CusADi2: Latency-Optimized Batch Computation of Robot Kinematics, Jacobians, and Hessians on the GPU
papers.summary: Trajectory optimization methods, from sampling-based zero-order to gradient-based first- and second-order approaches, require many evaluations of dynamical system functions, i.e., functions derived from a robot's dynamical model, such as forward kinematics and their Jacobians and Hessians. These evaluations are largely independent, e.g., across sampled trajectories or time steps, and can thus be evaluated in parallel as a batch. When used to make decisions online, these methods require low latency, i.e., each batch must complete in as little wall-clock time as possible. Existing frameworks utilize modern GPU hardware primarily to parallelize across batch instances, thereby optimizing throughput but not latency. We present CusADi2, a software library that reduces the batch evaluation latency by additionally parallelizing computation within each batch instance. We benchmark forward kinematics, Jacobians, and Hessians for all 67~robots in the MuJoCo Menagerie, including arms, hands, quadrupeds, humanoids, and biomechanical models, against MuJoCo XLA, MuJoCo Warp, frax, CusADi, and CasADi. CusADi2 achieves lower latency than all baselines at batch sizes of 64 to 4096, while matching them at larger batch sizes. We also demonstrate the performance advantage of CusADi2 in a sampling-based control application. All code is open-source at: https://github.com/johnviljoen/cusadi2
papers.title_ja: CusADi2: GPU上でのロボット運動学、ヤコビアン、ヘッシアンのレイテンシ最適化バッチ計算
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、GPU上でロボットの運動学やヤコビアン、ヘッシアンのバッチ計算のレイテンシを低減するソフトウェアライブラリCusADi2を提案する。既存のフレームワークがバッチ間の並列化（スループット最適化）に焦点を当てていたのに対し、CusADi2はバッチ内の計算も並列化することで、オンライン決定に必要な低レイテンシを実現する。MuJoCo Menagerieの67種のロボットモデルを用いたベンチマークにおいて、バッチサイズ64〜4096の範囲で既存の基線手法（MuJoCo XLA, Warp, frax, CusADi, CasADi）よりも低いレイテンシを示した。さらに、サンプリングベースの制御アプリケーションにおける性能向上も実証されている。
papers.relevance_reason: GPU並列化と最適化手法は関連するが、対象がロボット運動学であり軌道力学ではないため

papers.title: Scenario Generalization and Sector Transfer in Real Surface Irrigation Surrogate Modelling with Tabular Models
papers.summary: Surface irrigation planning requires screening many operating conditions and spatial configurations, while high-fidelity shallow-water-equation (SWE) simulations are expensive. We study tabular surrogate models for predicting maximum water height from drone-derived field morphology, terrain, hydrological, spatial, and scenario descriptors, where each row represents a spatial cell under one irrigation scenario. To assess deployment feasibility, we evaluate gradient-boosted trees, neural tabular models, AutoML, and tabular foundation models (TFMs) under two regimes: same-sector generalization, where a model predicts unseen scenarios after observing a limited set of configurations in the same sector, and sector-out transfer, where knowledge learned from source sectors is transferred to an unseen sector. The main findings are twofold: a) under the evaluated fixed 8/32 same-sector split, surrogates achieve strong performance, especially with raw spatial coordinates; b) sector-out transfer is substantially harder because the target sector has different coordinates and geometry. Sector-frame normalization of spatial coordinates improves transfer across similarly structured sectors, but does not solve cross-shape generalization. Overall, tabular surrogates appear useful for same-sector scenario screening under this fixed split, while robust transfer to unseen sectors remains open.
papers.title_ja: 表層灌漑サロゲートモデリングにおけるシナリオ汎化とセクター間転移（表形式モデルを用いた実地表面での研究）
papers.summary_ja: 高コストな浅水方程式シミュレーションの代替として、ドローンデータから得られる地形・水文情報を用いた表形式サロゲートモデルを構築し、最大水位の予測精度を評価した。グラディエントブースティングやニューラルネットワーク、AutoML、表形式ファウンデーションモデル（TFM）を比較し、同一セクター内でのシナリオスクリーニングでは高い性能を示すことを確認した。一方、異なる幾何構造を持つ未見のセクターへの知識転移は困難であり、座標正規化による改善効果には限界があることが判明した。本手法は、限られた設定条件下での灌漑計画の高速化に有用だが、汎用的な空間転移には課題が残る。
papers.relevance_reason: サロゲートモデルとML手法の適用だが、対象が灌漑であり軌道力学とは無関係

papers.title: Optimal Multi-Kernel Combination for Online Multi-Label Classification
papers.summary: Multi-label classification is particularly challenging in streaming scenarios, where data arrives sequentially. Online kernel methods offer a promising solution. However, prevailing methods rely on a single preselected kernel, making them prone to suboptimal choices since the global data distribution is unknown in advance in online settings. Although the recent method, Online Kernel Selection for Online Multi-label Classification (OKS-OMC), enables data-driven kernel selection, it fails to fully harness the complementary information from multiple kernels and encounters the curse of kernelization. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel online multi-kernel combination method for large-scale multi-label classification. First, an efficient and robust online single-kernel multi-label method is designed. Second, learning an optimal convex combination of multiple multi-label kernel classifiers is formalized as a structural risk minimization problem. An improved alternating optimization procedure is developed, in which the combination coefficients are updated by directly minimizing the objective function, while each kernel classifier is updated by minimizing a surrogate upper bound. This procedure decouples the learning of kernel classifiers from combination coefficients, allowing independent classifier updates via our single-kernel method and accelerating convergence to high-quality solutions. Our multi-kernel method is proven to asymptotically converge to the optimal fixed convex combination of the best fixed single-kernel models chosen in hindsight. Ablation studies confirm that our method's components outperform their counterparts in OKS-OMC. Comprehensive evaluations across 11 datasets and seven metrics demonstrate our method's overall superiority over existing online multi-label methods.
papers.title_ja: オンラインマルチラベル分類における最適なマルチカーネル結合
papers.summary_ja: ストリーミング環境におけるマルチラベル分類の課題に対し、単一カーネルの限界を克服するオンラインマルチカーネル結合手法を提案する。構造リスク最小化問題として定式化し、カーネル分類器と結合係数の学習を分離する改良版交互最適化手順を開発した。この手法は、事後に選択される最良の固定単一カーネルモデルの最適な凸結合に漸近的に収束することを理論的に証明している。11データセットでの評価により、既存手法を上回る性能と収束速度の向上を実証した。
papers.relevance_reason: カーネル法とオンライン学習はML手法全般に該当するが、軌道力学やLLM特化ではないため中程度。

papers.title: A Simple and Unified Method for Gradient-Variation Regret
papers.summary: Gradient-variation online learning has attracted increasing attention for its connections to game theory and optimization. It has been studied in both non-stationary online learning, which aims to minimize dynamic regret against time-varying comparator sequences, and universal online learning, which seeks to adapt to unknown loss curvature. Prior work obtained gradient-variation bounds using different techniques tailored to each setting. We propose a simple and unified method based on surrogate losses with a quadratic penalty on decision movement, yielding gradient-variation bounds in both settings. For non-stationary online learning, the method induces an optimistic-to-gradient-variation reduction, enabling a broad class of algorithms to match the rate established by Zhao et al. (2024). For universal online learning, it yields a simple algorithm that matches the optimal universal regret bounds of Yan et al. (2024) while relaxing the extended smoothness assumption. Finally, we apply our method to online games and improve on existing guarantees.
papers.title_ja: 勾配変動リグレットに対する単純かつ統一された手法
papers.summary_ja: 勾配変動オンライン学習において、非定常環境と普遍的オンライン学習の両方で勾配変動リグレットの境界を導出する統一手法を提案する。決定変更に二次ペナルティを課すサロゲート損失を用いることで、既存の個別手法を統合し、より広いアルゴリズムクラスで最適な速度比を達成する。さらに、拡張滑らか性仮定を緩和しつつ最適な普遍的リグレット境界を維持し、オンラインゲームにおける保証も改善する。
papers.relevance_reason: オンライン最適化の理論的進展であり、ML手法全般に関わるが、LLMや軌道力学との直接の関連は薄い。

papers.title: ZeroDSS: Semantic Segmentation from Class Names Alone
papers.summary: Semantic segmentation depends heavily on real images with pixel-level annotations, making dense supervision a major obstacle to deployment in new domains. We study task-specific data-free semantic segmentation, where training uses generic pretrained generative priors but has access to no target-domain images, masks, or captions--only a predefined category set. We introduce Zero-Data Semantic Segmentation (ZeroDSS), a feedback-driven approach that treats synthetic supervision as an adaptively controllable training distribution rather than a direct surrogate for real data. ZeroDSS constructs a semantically structured prompt distribution through LLM-guided compositional generation and adaptive class rebalancing, then converts the prompts into image-mask pairs using diffusion attention. Its feedback-driven distribution refinement consists of a two-phase closed-loop training procedure with a single loop-back step. In Phase I, a segmenter is trained using confidence-weighted supervision and dual-scale consistency. In Phase II, model feedback is used to adaptively target underperforming categories and refine diffusion-derived masks using model predictions. After this refined initial training, a teacher-student framework is utilized in the final phase to iteratively improve the fused supervision and segmenter through exponential moving average (EMA) updates. Using synthetic training data only, ZeroDSS achieves 35.0% mIoU on MS COCO with DeepLabV3, and 66.3% and 63.5% mIoU on PASCAL VOC with DeepLabV3 and Mask2Former, respectively. These results show that explicitly constructing and iteratively refining the synthetic supervision distribution can substantially reduce the synthetic-to-real gap in dense prediction.
papers.title_ja: ZeroDSS: クラス名のみから行うセマンティックセグメンテーション
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、ターゲットドメインの画像やアノテーションが一切不要なデータフリーなセマンティックセグメンテーション手法「ZeroDSS」を提案する。LLMによる構造化プロンプト生成と拡散モデルを用いた合成データ作成、およびモデルのフィードバックに基づく分布の適応的改善を行う。このフィードバック駆動型のアプローチにより、合成データと実データ間のギャップを縮小し、MS COCOで35.0% mIoU、PASCAL VOCで66.3% mIoUという高い性能を達成した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM活用と深層学習手法を含むが、軌道力学や推論高速化という核心関心とは乖離があるため。

papers.title: Language-Forcing: Advancing Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Semantic Alignment of Whole-Body World Action Models
papers.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict robot actions and future observations. However, their visual prediction objectives do not explicitly distinguish task-relevant transitions from incidental scene changes. For whole-body policies, this distinction matters because task progress depends on coordinated changes in body pose, contact, and object state. We introduce LANGUAGE-FORCING, a training strategy that uses language to emphasize task-relevant changes in the future visual representations of a whole-body WAM. Given paired current and ground- truth short-horizon future frames, a frozen vision-language model assesses task progress and predicts plausible subsequent state changes. We encode these descriptions with a frozen text encoder and align their embeddings with intermediate, action-conditioned future-visual features, complementing the original visual and action prediction objectives. All auxiliary components are used only during training, introducing no additional inference overhead. On HumanoidArena, LANGUAGE-FORCING achieves an average success rate of 79.17%, exceeding the strongest competing policy by 9.46 percentage points and the same WAM without language alignment by 10.77 percentage points. Across five real-world tasks, language alignment raises average success from 53.33% to 71.33% over the same WAM baseline.
papers.title_ja: Language-Forcing: 全身ワールドアクションモデルのセマンティックアラインメントによるヒューマノイドの歩行・操作性能向上
papers.summary_ja: ヒューマノイドロボットの全身制御において、ワールドアクションモデル（WAM）の視覚予測がタスク関連の変化と無関係なシーン変化を区別しにくい問題を解決する手法を提案する。凍結されたビジョン言語モデルを用いてタスク進捗を評価し、そのテキスト埋め込みをWAMの中間特徴量とアラインメントさせることで、推論時の計算コストを増やさずに学習精度を向上させる。HumanoidArenaベンチマークでは競合手法を上回る79.17%の成功率を達成し、実環境でも成功率を大幅に改善した。
papers.relevance_reason: LLM活用とエージェント設計に関わるが、対象がロボット制御であり軌道力学とは無関係

papers.title: Unified Multiparadigm Fusion Intelligence for Rare Disease Diagnosis
papers.summary: Rare diseases (RDs) affect an estimated 300 million people globally, leaving patients to navigate a protracted diagnostic odyssey constrained by clinical scarcity and fragmented medical knowledge. Artificial intelligence (AI) has progressively advanced RD diagnostics, from symbolic methods and deep learning to large language model (LLM)-based systems. However, each paradigm carries structural limitations: symbolic methods are bounded by knowledge completeness, neural models sacrifice interpretability, and LLM-based systems are vulnerable to evaluation biases like data leakage. In this study, we introduce FusionRare, a unified multiparadigm fusion framework integrating knowledge-driven symbolic reasoning, deep-learning pattern recognition, case-based patient retrieval, and LLM-based heuristic inference via statistical meta-aggregation and knowledge-enhanced agentic reflection. Evaluated on 2,528 strictly isolated clinical cases, FusionRare achieves state-of-the-art RD prioritization, attaining a macro-averaged Recall @1 of 51% for phenotype-only diagnosis and 79% for phenotype-genotype joint analysis. These results represent decisive advantages over the advanced agentic system DeepRare, frontier LLMs including GPT 5.5, and specialized tools like PhenoBrain and LIRICAL under stringent anti-leakage protocols. A randomized, crossover clinician-AI validation demonstrated that FusionRare elevates the true diagnostic rank in 45% of decisions, improves physician confidence in 62%, and reduces time to diagnosis by 21%. These findings indicate that reconciling these orthogonal AI paradigms significantly enhances diagnostic capabilities, bridging the gap between computational benchmarks and actionable clinical reliability. More broadly, this work provides a replicable framework for deploying trustworthy diagnostic AI across complex, high-stakes, and underserved medical domains.
papers.title_ja: 希少疾患診断のための統合型マルチパラダイム融合インテリジェンス
papers.summary_ja: 希少疾患の診断精度向上を目的とし、記号推論、深層学習、ケースベース推論、LLMベースの推論を統合したフレームワーク「FusionRare」を提案する。統計的メタ集約と知識強化型エージェントリフレクションにより、データリークを厳密に制御した評価で既存の最先端システムやGPT 5.5を上回る性能を達成した。臨床医とのクロスオーバー検証では、診断順位向上や診断時間短縮などの実務的な利点も確認された。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMエージェント設計と評価手法の知見は有用だが、医療特化であり軌道力学やサロゲートモデルとの直接の関連は薄い。

papers.title: Do LMs Know What Variables Do? Interpreting Code Representations via Variable Roles
papers.summary: Variable roles describe recurring behaviors such as accumulation, traversal, and retaining the best candidate encountered. We use Sajaniemi's independently defined taxonomy to study which role distinctions can be recovered from large language models, how sparse autoencoders (SAEs) retain those distinctions, and whether associated directions support control of generation. We introduce static annotation rules for all eleven roles and a corpus of 126,926 natural-code files across five languages. Across five model-SAE systems, residual probes outperform individual SAE features and tested lexical baselines, with modest losses after neutral target renaming. Combining SAE features closes much of the single-feature gap, but probes on SAE reconstructions are less sensitive to role-changing edits reviewed by LLMs. High paired ranking accuracy coexists with frequent false positives at fixed thresholds. During generation, interventions often change role annotations at the cost of correctness; changes accompanied by passing tests show no clear aggregate advantage over random controls. The benchmark separates role-related recoverability, SAE fidelity, and correctness-preserving control through matched prediction, source edits, and generation interventions.
papers.title_ja: LLMは変数の役割を理解しているのか？変数役割を通じたコード表現の解釈
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）がコード内の「変数役割」（蓄積、走査など）をどの程度理解しているかを、スパースオートエンコーダ（SAE）を用いて分析した研究である。12万ファイル以上のコーパスを用いた評価では、残差プローブが個々のSAE特徴量よりも役割の識別に優れることが示された。しかし、生成時の介入は役割の注釈を変えつつも正解率を損なう傾向があり、テスト合格を伴う明確な改善は確認されなかった。本論文は、役割の復元可能性、SAEの忠実度、正解性を保つ制御の3軸でベンチマークを分離する手法を提案している。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの内部表現解釈とSAEという手法に関心があるが、コード特化であり軌道力学やRAGとは直接無関係。

papers.title: Forecasting Patient Trajectories from the Electronic Health Records with Action-Conditioned World Models
papers.summary: We introduce a predictive world model for electronic health records (EHR) that represents patient histories as action conditioned latent trajectories. Rather than modeling clinical events solely through autoregressive token prediction, our framework explicitly separates patient states from observed clinical actions and learns their evolution through a state and action conditioned transition operator. At its core is a state dependent linearization predictor that propagates local changes in latent patient state, enabling time resolved prediction, multi step rollout, and action conditioned simulation. Empirically, we show that generated latent trajectories preserve downstream predictive signal, temporal structure, and subgroup level statistical relationships present in encoder derived representations. We further decode free running rollouts into the original clinical feature space and evaluate future clinical measurements against observed values using task matched forecasting baselines, demonstrating that the learned dynamics retain predictive information beyond latent space agreement. Across binary classification and time to event tasks, EHR WM achieves competitive, though task dependent, performance relative to substantially larger EHR foundation models while using a 30x smaller parameter footprint. Finally, perturbing observed action sequences produces corresponding changes in generated trajectories, demonstrating the action sensitivity of the learned dynamics. Together, these results support world modeling as a complementary framework for learning explicit, time indexed representations of patient evolution from longitudinal EHR.
papers.title_ja: 行動条件付きワールドモデルを用いた電子カルテからの患者軌道の予測
papers.summary_ja: 電子カルテ（EHR）データにおいて、患者の状態と臨床行動を分離し、状態・行動条件付き遷移演算子によって潜在軌道を学習する予測ワールドモデルを提案する。状態依存の線形化予測器により、時間分解能のある予測や複数ステップのロールアウト、行動条件付きシミュレーションを実現する。大幅に小さいパラメータ数（30分の1）でありながら、大規模なEHR基盤モデルと比較して競合する性能を示し、行動の摂動に対する軌道の感度も検証されている。
papers.relevance_reason: 軌道力学ではないが、状態遷移とサロゲートモデルの手法が関連

papers.title: From Likelihood to Utility: Quality-Axis Diffusion for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.summary: Diffusion models have become a dominant paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet existing planners organize trajectory generation along the Gaussian-noise axis, treating driving utility only as an auxiliary guidance or selection signal. We instead formulate diffusion along a driving-quality axis. We propose QualiDrive, which constructs scene-specific quality ladders by ranking observed trajectories according to measured driving utility and learns to reverse this ordered degradation through ordered low-to-high-quality refinement. Each reverse step is conditioned on the scene, ego state, current trajectory, and target quality level, progressively refining trajectories toward higher driving quality. On NAVSIM, QualiDrive achieves 94.5 PDMS on v1 and a state-of-the-art 92.74 EPDMS on v2. QualiDrive improves Oracle EPDMS only modestly over endpoint-only quality supervision (98.52 to 98.57), but substantially increases the fractions of candidates above 0.95 and 0.98 EPDMS from 12.94%/9.71% to 21.53%/15.93%, raising selected EPDMS from 92.63 to 92.74. These results suggest that diffusion is not merely a process of denoising, but one of progressive quality-ordered refinement.
papers.title_ja: 尤度から効用へ：エンドツーエンド自動運転のための品質軸拡散モデル
papers.summary_ja: 既存の自動運転向け拡散モデルがガウスノイズ軸で軌道を生成するのに対し、本論文は「運転品質」を軸とした新しい拡散プロセスを提案する。観測された軌道を測定された効用に基づいてランキングし、低品質から高品質へ段階的に改善する「QualiDrive」手法を開発した。NAVSIMベンチマークにおいて、SOTA級の性能（EPDMS 92.74）を達成し、高品質候補の割合を大幅に向上させた。この結果は、拡散モデルが単なるノイズ除去ではなく、品質順序付けされた漸進的改善プロセスとして機能し得ることを示唆している。
papers.relevance_reason: 拡散モデルというML手法と軌道生成の組み合わせだが、宇宙軌道設計とは分野が異なるため中程度。

papers.title: InJePA: Intention-First Latent Planning with Coupled JEPA World Models for Visual Navigation
papers.summary: Visual navigation requires goal directed planning informed by predictions of environment dynamics. Representative navigation world model methods propose complete action candidates before predicting consequences for selection or search updates. For each candidate, predictions primarily evaluate proposed actions rather than guide its stepwise construction. To this end, we propose InJepa, an intention first planning paradigm centered on latent states. A goal conditioned JEPA proposes latent intentions, and an action conditioned JEPA continually predicts future latent states. Both operate in a shared latent space to align their predictive representations. Within each candidate, predicted consequences feed into the next intention proposal and action inference, forming a closed loop of intention, action, and consequence. This extends the world model's role beyond evaluation to leading candidate construction through latent intentions. We evaluate InJepa through closed loop image goal navigation in Habitat MP3D. The results show effective multistep navigation through intention guided action generation and consequence feedback. Experiments across encoders further support applicability across visual representations. These findings support latent intentions as the central planning object and show that world models can directly guide plan construction through coordinated reasoning about intentions and consequences. Code is available at https://github.com/zhuxun132/InJepa.
papers.title_ja: InJePA: 視覚ナビゲーションにおける結合型JEPA世界モデルを用いた意図優先の潜在計画
papers.summary_ja: 視覚ナビゲーションにおいて、従来の世界モデルが候補アクションの評価に留まる問題を解決するため、潜在空間での「意図」を計画の中心とする新パラダイムInJePAを提案する。目標条件付きJEPAが潜在意図を提案し、アクション条件付きJEPAが未来の潜在状態を予測することで、意図・アクション・結果の閉ループを形成する。Habitat MP3D環境での評価により、この手法がマルチステップナビゲーションにおいて有効であり、エンコーダの種類を問わず適用可能であることを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習・世界モデルの手法だが、軌道力学やLLM効率化との直接的な関連は薄い

papers.title: Fast Construction of Inner Sphere Trees Using Machine Learning
papers.summary: Collision detection for complex non-convex objects is a bottleneck in physics simulation, virtual reality, and robotics. Inner sphere trees (ISTs) answer proximity and penetration queries efficiently, but their greedy leaf-sphere construction is sequential and computationally expensive, which limits both large-scale preprocessing and runtime use. In this work, we present ML-IST, a machine-learning-based method that reformulates leaf-sphere generation as a single-shot set-prediction problem: a network predicts a fixed set of inscribed sphere candidates from multichannel voxel geometry, differentiable coverage feedback corrects the coarse prediction and fills residual gaps at finer scales, and a lightweight geometric projection enforces validity. Averaged over the test set, a single-GPU implementation of ML-IST reduces mean leaf-generation time by a factor of $2.0$--$2.6$ over single-core CPU construction across target capacities of 64--512 spheres, and qualitative results on complex models show multiscale sphere distributions that follow principal volumes and slender features. We further integrate ML-IST into the Jolt Physics and Bullet engines; in an alpha-puzzle benchmark it reaches 55.89~FPS, the highest among the compared representations (conventional IST, GImpact, and convex decomposition). These results support learned leaf generation as a practical component for fast, runtime construction of detailed collision representations.
papers.title_ja: 機械学習を用いた内部球ツリーの高速構築
papers.summary_ja: 複雑な非凸物体の衝突検出におけるボトルネックである内部球ツリー（IST）の構築を高速化するために、機械学習手法ML-ISTを提案する。ネットワークによる一発のセット予測と微分可能なカバレッジフィードバックを用いることで、従来の逐次構築より2.0〜2.6倍高速にリーフ球を生成できる。Jolt PhysicsやBulletエンジンへの統合により、既存手法を上回るフレームレートを実現し、リアルタイム物理シミュレーションへの実用性を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: ML活用と高速化は関心だが、対象が物理シミュレーションであり軌道力学とは無関係

papers.title: Physics-Aware Self-Supervised Pretraining on Multi-Domain Raman Spectra
papers.summary: Raman spectroscopy generates large volumes of unlabeled data that are difficult to exploit with conventional supervised learning. This work introduces a multi-domain self-supervised learning framework based on a masked autoencoder (MAE) for learning transferable Raman spectral representations from heterogeneous biological, chemical, forensic, and materials datasets. The proposed pretraining strategy incorporates physics-aware objectives by combining masked intensity reconstruction with a sparse Voigt-profile decoder that models spectral peak structure through differentiable peak centers, widths, and amplitudes. A denoising objective is further included to improve robustness to spectral corruption. The learned encoder is evaluated on substance classification, component identification, concentration estimation, and spectral denoising under linear probing, attention-based probing, end-to-end fine-tuning, and training from scratch. Experimental results show that self-supervised pretraining is most beneficial for challenging tasks with limited labeled data. Attention-based probing also reveals substantially more useful information in the frozen representation than linear probing, indicating that conventional linear evaluation may underestimate representation quality. In addition, the benefits of pretraining become more pronounced with increasing encoder capacity. Overall, the proposed framework demonstrates that physics-aware, multi-domain self-supervised pretraining can improve label efficiency, robustness, and transferability across diverse Raman spectroscopy tasks.
papers.title_ja: 多領域ラマン分光スペクトルにおける物理認識型自己教師あり事前学習
papers.summary_ja: ラマン分光スペクトルの大量の無ラベルデータを活用するため、マスクオートエンコーダ（MAE）ベースの自己教師あり事前学習フレームワークを提案する。物理法則を反映した目的関数として、強度再構成に加え、スペクトルピーク構造をモデル化するスパースなヴォイグトプロファイルデコーダとノイズ除去目的関数を組み込む。生物・化学・法科学・材料などの異種データセットで学習したエンコーダは、物質分類や濃度推定などのタスクにおいて、特にラベルデータが少ない場合に高い効率性と汎化性能を示した。また、線形プロービングよりもアテンションベースのプロービングの方が表現の質をより正確に評価できることが明らかになった。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理情報と自己教師あり学習の組み合わせは関連するが、対象が分光スペクトルであり軌道力学ではないため中程度。

papers.title: SPADE-KD: Peer-to-Peer Collaborative Learning under Heterogeneous Settings
papers.summary: Peer-to-peer collaborative learning is an emerging distributed deep learning paradigm that eliminates the need for a central aggregator and disseminator, avoiding the single-point-of-failure and bottleneck issues they can bring. Many such approaches use parameter averaging, requiring clients to have homogeneous model architectures, whereas others use knowledge distillation as an alternative while leaning on shared public data or centralized control infrastructure. Many of these approaches also make a one-size-fits-all assumption, i.e., jointly training a single, globally optimal solution for all clients, when in reality, clients' underlying data distributions might differ such that a globally optimal solution may not be locally optimal for all clients. To enable collaborative learning in environments with both model architecture and data distribution heterogeneity, we present SPADE-KD -- a fully decentralized model distillation framework that optimizes collaboration towards personalized rather than global performance. SPADE-KD leverages two mechanisms -- adaptive distillation and utility-driven peer selection. Adaptive distillation modulates the strength of each incoming model transfer by the performance advantage of the incoming model compared to the native model measured by their task losses, such that a client will distill more aggressively from incoming models that outperform it on its own local data. Utility-driven peer selection uses the loss-informed utility derived from adaptive distillation to rank prospective partners, focusing on exchanges that measurably improve the local model while suppressing low-utility transfers. Using federated classification tasks, we demonstrate that SPADE-KD consistent outperforms naive decentralized distillation with lower loss and faster convergence and that its individual components are more effective together than independently.

papers.title: Injection of Space Radiation Errors on Low-power NVM using Generative Deep Learning
papers.summary: We develop an error model for a Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) device that represents the effects of physical faults experienced in a CubeSat mission in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). We visually analyze erroneous values distributions in the memory snapshots and we understand that they are frequently distributed according to regular spatial patterns. We define a generative deep learning technique to automatically learn these spatial patterns and to synthetically generate additional error patterns mimicking the observed ones. The model is capable at producing memory errors for general application-level experimentation. Our preliminary validation indicates that when comparing the model output with the data we collect, 0.92 of the generated bit flips correspond to bit flips in the memory snapshots and the model captures 0.91 of the observed bit flips. A comparison of the spatial distribution of bit flips in 10,000 generated error patterns also provides a Wasserstein distance of 0.073, indicating that the two distributions differ by roughly 7% of the maximum possible displacement of their probability masses.

papers.title: Beyond Explicit Intent: Discovering and Shaping Artistic Intent through Human-AI Co-Creation
papers.summary: Generative AI is becoming an important medium for artistic creation, yet existing interactions often assume that creators can specify intentions in advance and accurately communicate them through text prompts. By expanding model exploration, we expose artists to diverse visual possibilities, allowing them to identify previously unarticulated preferences through observation, comparison, and selection. We then integrate artists' curatorial judgments into reinforcement learning, assigning different learning strengths based on preferences over generation trajectories, so recognized directions are more strongly reinforced and the model gradually adapts to individual aesthetics. This creates a continuous "explore-identify-shape-re-explore" loop in which artistic intent is progressively discovered, externalized, and shaped. Through three user studies, we examine latent-preference discovery, personalized preference alignment, and the externalization of vague, difficult-to-express creative intentions.

papers.title: SECURE-AI: Multi-Signal Uncertainty Quantification for Trustworthy Acoustic Cough Detection
papers.summary: Acoustic models for cough detection achieve high accuracy on curated benchmarks but fail silently in deployment, where speech, environmental noise, and audio unlike the training data induce confident misclassifications. In health monitoring, a confidently wrong prediction is worse than no answer at all. We present SECURE-AI (Self-aware Estimation of Cough Uncertainty for Reliable Evaluation of AI), a multi-signal uncertainty quantification framework that wraps a frozen MobileNetV3 cough classifier and estimates when its predictions should not be trusted, combining Monte Carlo Dropout, Temperature Scaling, and Mahalanobis distance in the embedding space. On a held-out split of 12,161 Coswara recordings, the probability-space methods are individually insufficient: Monte Carlo Dropout assigns lower uncertainty to incorrect than to correct predictions, and temperature scaling improves calibration but not discrimination. The strongest signal is embedding-space distance: Mahalanobis distance separates true positives from false positives (means 44.7 versus 63.4; Cohen's $d = 0.94$; AUROC 0.86) and, among predicted non-coughs, false negatives from true negatives (AUROC 0.82), so the same signal can flag both false alarms and missed coughs. At a descriptive operating point selected from labeled test data, retaining 90 percent of true-positive detections removes about two-thirds of false positives and raises precision from 59.9 to roughly 80 percent. A rejection threshold tuned on one split does not transfer to another (validation F1 of 82 percent falls to 34 percent on test), so we report threshold-independent AUROC as the main measure. An error taxonomy shows that failures are systematic, with most false positives related to speech. The pipeline runs on Raspberry Pi hardware costing 30 to 90 US dollars. Probabilistic calibration alone is thus inadequate for reliable cough detection.

papers.title: A Group-Aware Comparative Study of Classical Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods for Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition
papers.summary: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) using wearable or smartphone inertial sensors is commonly evaluated with both classical machine learning and deep learning methods. However, reported performance can be strongly affected by sensor modality, dataset characteristics, and data-splitting strategy. This study presents a controlled comparative evaluation of four classical machine learning models and four deep learning models on two public HAR datasets, UCI-HAR and KU-HAR. Three sensor modalities were considered: accelerometer (ACC), gyroscope (GYRO), and their combination (ACC+GYRO). Classical machine learning models used handcrafted statistical features, while deep learning models operated directly on raw sensor sequences. The primary evaluation employed five-fold StratifiedGroupKFold cross-validation, with subject- or participant-level grouping to prevent group overlap between training and test folds. Macro-F1 was used as the primary performance metric. The results show that deep learning did not consistently outperform classical machine learning. On UCI-HAR, the evaluated deep learning models achieved slightly higher macro-F1 values, whereas on KU-HAR, LightGBM achieved 0.857 compared with 0.828 for the highest-performing evaluated deep learning model. Regarding sensor modality, the combined ACC+GYRO configuration generally outperformed ACC or GYRO alone on both datasets. The evaluation protocol also had a substantial effect: for CNNBiLSTMAttn with ACC+GYRO, random splitting increased macro-F1 by 0.033 on UCI-HAR and 0.093 on KU-HAR compared with grouped evaluation. These findings highlight the importance of model family, sensor modality, dataset characteristics, and group-aware evaluation when assessing sensor-based HAR systems.
papers.title_ja: センサベースの人間活動認識における古典的機械学習と深層学習手法のグループ認識型比較研究

papers.title: REAP: Learning General Rearrangement Heuristics from Motion-Planner Feedback
papers.summary: Robotic rearrangement tasks require planning sequences of actions that fulfill high-level specifications while also being geometrically feasible. Symbolic abstractions make the combinatorial structure of rearrangement tasks tractable, but they usually do not fully capture the geometric constraints that determine which actions a robot can actually realize. These constraints are hard to express in the symbolic model. We propose REAP (Rearrangement with Elicited Action Preconditions), a framework in which a relational graph neural network heuristic is learned over a simple symbolic abstraction. A motion planner serves as a supervisor that elicits the hidden geometric preconditions of the problem during training. Deployed with greedy best-first search, the learned heuristic generalizes out-of-distribution along object count, plan length, and object arrangement, and can be trained jointly on several domains. Compared to classical heuristic search and learning-based baselines, REAP solves more problems, requires roughly an order of magnitude fewer motion-planner queries than comparable methods, and the action it ranks first is geometrically feasible in 94% of sampled states, against 22% for a random choice.
papers.title_ja: REAP: モーションプランナーのフィードバックから汎用的な再配置ヒューリスティクスを学習する

papers.title: Weakly Supervised Discovery of Motion Styles for Compositional Robot Control
papers.summary: When a robot possesses more degrees of freedom than a task requires, multiple trajectories can achieve the same objective using distinct motion styles. Compositional robot control aims to preserve a selected style while simultaneously executing an independent task command, effectively balancing these potentially competing objectives. In this paper, we present CODES, a framework for compositional robot control that discovers a coherent style repertoire from diverse recordings and composes it with independent commands. First, motion retargeting maps the recordings to motions executable by the target robot; next, weakly supervised consensus encoding and density-based clustering identify styles within and across recordings without a prescribed count; finally, reinforcement learning trains a policy to compose the discovered styles with independent commands. We evaluate CODES on a Unitree Go2 quadruped across two simulators and physical hardware. Compared to baselines, CODES significantly improves kinematic coherence. Furthermore, our controller successfully tracks velocity commands that generalize beyond the support of the recorded data, exhibiting robust and distinguishable style characteristics during both cross-simulator and real-world hardware deployments. papers.title: Improving Fake Profile Detection Through Multimodal Learning and Research-Guided Feature Integration
papers.summary: Fake accounts continue to undermine online platforms, yet it remains unclear whether multimodal learning offers meaningful improvements over strong metadata baselines or graph-based approaches. We propose a multimodal framework combining pretrained textual (XLM-RoBERTa) and visual (CLIP) embeddings with structured account-level features such as follower counts, posting frequency, and account age, and evaluate multiple modality combinations using CatBoost alongside a Relational Graph Convolutional Network (R-GCN). Results show that metadata alone is highly predictive, while multimodal fusion yields only marginal and largely statistically insignificant gains. The graph-based model underperforms classical variants under the subsampled graph conditions of this study. Overall, our findings suggest that under practical constraints, feature quality and metadata richness matter more than fusion complexity.

papers.title: Pack and Extract: An Effective Graph-Based Approach for Feature Selection
papers.summary: Many molecular biology data sets contain thousands of features, such as genes in single-cell experiments or other omics data. In this paper, we propose an improvement to IDS-based feature selection that (i) favors features exhibiting greater diversity and (ii) generalizes the notion of independent dominating set to a node packing model. We evaluate our approach on five genetic data sets and compare the results with those obtained using existing methods. Our experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in predictive accuracy over traditional models, as well as increased stability of the selected feature sets.

papers.title: Proton acceleration at interplanetary shocks: A numerical study for the HENON mission
papers.summary: The ESA-ASI HENON CubeSat mission will operate in a distant retrograde orbit about 0.08 au upstream of Earth to provide advance space-weather monitoring. Its instruments include an energetic particle detector measuring protons from 2 MeV to hundreds of MeV. Early detection of energetic particles is crucial for protecting technological infrastructure. To investigate proton acceleration at interplanetary shocks, we developed a test-particle numerical simulation in which protons move in the drift approximation around a parallel shock transition and gain energy through a first-order Fermi process at each crossing. They can propagate around the shock either diffusively or superdiffusively; particle transport affects shock acceleration. Protons were injected at the shock with an energy distribution of about 10 keV and scattered in pitch angle by a collision operator. We varied the pitch-angle scattering time, upstream and downstream plasma speeds, and the type of transport. In the superdiffusive case, a power-law distribution of scattering times was generated by mimicking a L\'evy walk. Multiple runs identify the parameter ranges that yield efficient acceleration and higher energies. For typical parameters, superdiffusive acceleration turns out to be somewhat faster than normal diffusive acceleration. We find that the main control parameter appears to be the upstream shock speed, and that energies in the range of 2-10 MeV can be reached for upstream speeds in the shock frame, $V_1$, of the order of 300 km/s or more. Conversely, for a speed of $V_1 \leq 150$ km/s the proton energy reaches only a few hundred keV. These results help explain why many interplanetary shocks accelerate ions only to moderate energies. They also suggest that when the HENON particle instrument is able to detect energetic protons above 2 MeV, the shock speed in the spacecraft frame is of the order of 800 km/s or more.

papers.title: DUET: Decoupled Upper- and Lower-Body Execution for Task-Agnostic Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.summary: Changing a humanoid robot's manipulation policy should not require retraining the controller that maintains the robot's balance. This study introduces DUET, a decoupled execution framework that enables locomotion and manipulation controllers to operate simultaneously by combining their commands only at the robot interface. A reinforcement-learning locomotion policy controls the 12 leg joints and a waist yaw joint, tracking planar velocity, turning rate, and pelvis height from deep crouching to upright standing on a 23-degree-of-freedom Unitree G1. The 10 arm joints are excluded from the action space, while their positions and velocities are included only as observations, so that any compatible manipulation policy that generates arm-joint targets can control the upper body, and the locomotion policy keeps the lower body stable without requiring shared training or direct coordination. This study demonstrates the modular approach on hardware by pairing the same locomotion checkpoint with two different vision-language-action models, GR00T N1.7 and pi0.5. In simulation evaluation, the locomotion controller kept the robot's lower body stable with no falls while tracking the commanded planar velocity, yaw rate, and pelvis height with errors of 0.186 m/s, 0.142 rad/s, and 0.016 m, respectively. Ablation studies identify the upper-body pose curriculum as the dominant component, and removing this training step reduces episode survival from 20.0 to 7.4 seconds and increases the fall rate to 6.06 per environment minute. Robustness tests show no falls under pushes of up to 1.0 m/s within the trained payload range, and no falls at twice the payload limit for pushes below 0.7 m/s. These results show that a manipulation policy can be exchanged without retraining, restarting, or otherwise touching the layer that keeps the robot upright.

papers.title: Announced Breaks Separate Conformal Reliability from Frequency Calibration
papers.summary: An announced boundary reveals the partition before the first affected outcome, and a reset there serves one of two audits. The per-time audit reads conformal reliability, the expected distance of the threshold's coverage from nominal at miscoverage 0.1. The frequency audit reads frequency calibration, whether a closed window's error rate matched it. The reset rule, the post-boundary empirical quantile, attains the minimax per-time rate for independent scores. On bounded scores a recursion reset at the boundary attains a frequency gap of order one over the count when its floor adds a bounded total. At the 50th forecast after a large synthetic break, the reset rule's per-time gap stands below that of five adaptive methods, four from their authors' code, with every paired band below zero. After an electricity market reform, on 68 unseen scores, the band stands below zero against two, includes zero against two, adaptive conformal inference among them, and is a point at zero against one. After monetary policy decisions its pointwise band stands above zero against all five on 10 of the first 34 days. Of 9 announced boundaries one clears the smallest coverage difference its window detects, where every method's per-time gap at the 50th forecast exceeds the nominal miscoverage. Over the first 50 forecasts the reset recursion leads the frequency audit after every synthetic break.
papers.title_ja: 告知された破断が、共形信頼性と周波数較正を分離する

papers.title: ChairNav: Cross-Embodiment Pre-training and Personalization for Long-Horizon Wheelchair Navigation
papers.summary: Developing autonomous electric wheelchairs capable of long-horizon sidewalk navigation is critical for accessible personal mobility, yet existing approaches either focus on indoor map-based navigation or rely on expensive, complex sensor stacks to achieve full autonomy. In this work, we propose to tackle outdoor sidewalk navigation by leveraging visual navigation foundation models and large-scale navigation datasets, which offer strong generalization using lightweight hardware. To this end, we present ChairNav, a novel framework that adapts a general visual navigation model into a personalized electric wheelchair navigation system using a three-stage data pyramid. To address the scarcity of in-domain data, ChairNav first pre-trains on large-scale cross-embodiment datasets transformed into the wheelchair domain, followed by mid-training on a small number of wheelchair demonstrations to eliminate remaining domain gaps. Finally, a post-training stage refines the deployed model from user interventions to personalize its behavior. We deploy ChairNav on a commercial electric wheelchair equipped with an RGB-D camera and an onboard NVIDIA Jetson compute module. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of each stage in our data pyramid: pre-training reduces lateral ADE by 18%, and post-training increases the mean distance between user interventions from 29.2 m to 57.4 m. Further evaluation on kilometer-scale urban sidewalk routes shows that our system operates autonomously for 93.4% of total driving time, demonstrating its potential for everyday accessible mobility. Demo video and more details are at https://vail.cs.ucla.edu/ChairNav/.

papers.title: The moduli space of quasimorphisms on subshifts and its pressure geometry
papers.summary: We introduce a metric geometry on the space of positive, linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing subshift of finite type. Two such quasimorphisms are identified when their homogenizations agree up to multiplicative scaling. The resulting moduli space carries a natural symmetrised Thurston-type metric, defined from the extremal ratios of their periodic orbit lengths. We prove that this is a genuine metric and determine several global features of the resulting space: it is unbounded, separable, incomplete, and has geodesics that are canonically generated by thermodynamic pressure functions. We then describe the endpoints of these geodesics and develop a boundary theory for our moduli space. We apply this theory to metric structures on right-angled Artin and Coxeter groups. In particular we construct isometric embeddings of geometric moduli spaces into our quasimorphism moduli spaces. As a consequence, Manhattan curves for metrics on these groups are $C^1$, with equality cases characterised by rough similarity of the underlying metrics. This provides insights into Manhattan curves in settings where neither classical thermodynamic formalism for H\"older potentials nor Patterson-Sullivan theory apply. The same construction recovers the corresponding results for hyperbolic groups and places these examples within a common dynamical-geometric framework.

papers.title: DISCERN: Identifiable Disease Evidence for Generalizable Medical Multimodal Learning
papers.summary: Clinical multimodal models can learn enrollment shortcuts shared across modalities and fail on new cohorts. We model these data through a latent structural causal model: disease state and background factors generate physiology through shared mechanisms, while cohorts differ in selection and measurement. Holding acquisition fixed, we identify conditional disease evidence without observing disease-state labels or recovering the full causal model. In common Gaussian coordinates, cross-cohort state alignment and natural-parameter changes identify a minimal selection statistic; conditioning on it removes enrollment-dependent evidence and yields an identifiable reference posterior within the specified shift family. State-dependent interactions can carry evidence invisible to individual-modality posteriors, motivating joint, information-preserving representations. DISCERN combines an information-lattice encoder, a latent-state model, and an outcome head through joint training. Under reversed synthetic enrollment on known latent coordinates, conditioning raises state AUROC from 0.043 to 0.883 and from 0.265 to 0.825, while random conditioning does not. Exploratory cross-database mortality experiments between eICU and MIMIC-IV improve AUROC over matched empirical risk minimization by 0.036 and 0.035. Learned-coordinate diagnostics distinguish preservation of state information from identification of the coordinates required by the estimator.
